ucas.description: A non-serving node stays Active.
A divergent replica remains eligible without repair.
Healthy copies are demoted on false or correlated failure observations.
A master is demoted before a usable successor exists.
A lone unhealthy master loses its assignment without a successor.
A live node remains Down indefinitely.
An empty or stale node is crowned master.
Multiple processes serve as master for a partition.
A masterless partition is never refilled.
A replica is activated or promoted before completing synchronization.
Deletion destroys the last usable copy.
Deletion interrupts reconstruction or repeats on a terminating pod.
Force deletion bypasses evidence and drain conditions.
Topology application is lost or never retried.
Delayed topology arrives after a newer authority or assignment.
A deposed leader still issues topology commands.
Repeated resync failure never removes an unsafe replica from serving.
Endpoint membership advertises an unserving node.
Fetch is not resumed after a transient disconnection.
The applied position advances past a range that was not applied (e.g. a forwarded write taken as WAL progress).
A newer value arrives by forwarding and an older WAL change is then applied over it.
A delete is applied and an older put then resurrects the key.
The process crashes after applying changes and before the position is saved, so the same range is re-applied or skipped inconsistently.
A batch from an old session or lineage is applied.
A replica whose required history is gone is treated as synchronised.
A lagging or unobservable replica is treated as safe for reads, promotion or deletion.
WAL is retained until the master's disk is exhausted.
Delete history is discarded while a change older than the delete can still be applied.
The apply decision is made against a position read before a stall, retry or lock wait, so a change admitted against an old cursor is written after the cursor moved.
After a rebuild, changes from the previous session, or metadata inherited from the source, are applied.
A key is changed by a path that does not capture an order label (bulk operation, internal delete), so the change cannot be ordered against the other delivery path.
A transient disconnection is treated as a repair trigger and starts a full reconstruction.
A partially initialised copy (metadata cleared, cursor or generation not yet written) accepts deliveries or is presented as a copy.

constraint.text: Only the current leader may issue topology changes; recipients must reject obsolete authority.

controls.title: Authorize topology application
scenarios: An old reconcile resumes after lease takeover; a node has not yet heard the new generation.
assumptions: Lease availability and generation identity must be established; a newer generation fences only recipients that have observed it.
residual_risks: A check before sending cannot close the check/send race: the lease can be lost between the read and the first packet, or while the broadcast is in flight.

Recipient-side version fencing only protects a node that has ALREADY observed the newer generation; a node that missed the new leader's broadcast will accept an older leader's map. Per-node applied-generation tracking is SAF-09.
The post-send lease re-read records that the race occurred; it cannot retract what was sent.

Observed while building CHECK-01, not asserted on: after the lease is deleted and the SAME process re-acquires it, the operator was seen broadcasting a LOWER version than nodes already held, which their fencing rejects. The manipulation is cruder than a real takeover; treat as a lead for SAF-09. ADDRESSED 2026-10-02 (CI pending): the generation came from Lease.transitions, which restarts when the Lease is deleted; a new leader now takes max(transitions, persisted generation + 1) and sends only versions already persisted (CHECK-01-generation).
The stop position is a test seam. It is inert without the environment variable and bounded at 120s, but it is production code that a misconfiguration could delay one broadcast with.

A suppressed send is retried only by a process that survives the suppression (lease read failure, momentarily foreign holder): the pending flag is in memory, and a confirmed lease loss ends the process, after which the next leader republishes from its own committed state. The retry test proves the flag was set by the withheld pass and consumed by the pass that published (that pass names the suppressed version); it does not prove the flag was NECESSARY for that send, because the committed version usually moves by itself within a pass.

Liveness (/healthz) is process-alive only and readiness treats a non-leader as ready. The operator that logged 'LOST LEASE -- exiting' and then hung — the Lean runtime waits for the never-ending server tasks before reporting the uncaught error — was therefore never restarted; that defect is fixed (IO.Process.exit) and CHECK-01 asserts the restart count moves, but a different stall of the main loop would still pass both probes.

The suite's evidence for 'the held pass did not send' is operator log lines read from the pod (across the designed restart); the checks are shape-based (fence for vHELD; a send line with old < new would be the held pass) rather than a wire-level capture. Two harness races (container replaced by the designed exit; retry line matching the negative check) were found by the CI runner's timing and fixed the same day; a third of the same family is plausible.

2026-10-01 (CI 36731888436): after the lease fence suppressed a broadcast, a newer commit superseded it before the retry, and the retry published the successor version instead of the withheld one; the test that names the suppressed version failed. Not data loss (survivors got the superseding map); the semantics of 'retry the withheld map' vs 'retry the current desired map' need the SAF-09 decision. RECLASSIFIED (2026-10-01): test premise, not a semantics gap. That pass was the restarted process's first, so its startup seed (v…306) was still pending when the fence withheld v…307; the flag keeps the earliest outstanding version and the retry publishes the latest committed map (documented design), so the line read pending v…306; publishing v…308. Test 4 now requires a retry line with pending ≤ held ≤ publishing. The FAIL record stays.

2026-10-01: the takeover test (b) ends on a check that every pod names the same master. Its held change is a read-balance weight, so the pre-takeover map already satisfies that check: it proves the exit and re-acquisition, not that the withheld map reached any pod or which path sent it. CHECK-01-startup adds the content and attribution check; the takeover test itself is unchanged.

Startup republish is tested only with the topology audit OFF (test seam FLARE_TEST_TOPOLOGY_AUDIT_OFF, inert when unset). With the audit on, a fresh process has two independent reasons to republish to a behind pod (startup seed, audit verdict=behind); the test shows the seed suffices, not how the two interact.

The send-reason record (broadcast trigger: ...) is logged with every send and is the attribution evidence; it is derived from the same four values the send condition uses (BroadcastTriggers.any), so it cannot disagree with the branch taken, but it is still a log line rather than a wire capture.

FINDING 2026-10-01 (CI 36831110279, not changed here): the persisted node map (serializeNodeMap) carries no read balance, so a reloaded map has every node at balance 100 until the first reconcile pass re-applies spec.readBalance and the SAF-10c read withholding. The operator answers node add from that in-memory map, and after a takeover the reloaded version is raised to the new generation base, newer than any pod holds. A flared pod that boots in that window adopts a map in which slaves, including WAL followers withheld from reads, carry balance 100, until the first pass pushes the corrected map seconds later. Running pods are not affected: flared requests the map only at boot. Side effect: with any slave weight other than 100, the first pass after a restart always advances the version, so the startup seed is rarely the only republish reason in practice. FIX (2026-10-01, CI pending): serializeNodeMap now persists each node's committed balance (balance=, including the SAF-10c withholding) and parseNodeMapLine restores it; a legacy line without the token loads as master 100 / others 0. Proved by nodeMapVersion_roundtrip (balances 100/0/25) and legacy_line_balance_fallback. The startup-republish E2E uses slave weight 25 again, so it fails if the reload changes the map.

Same-name replacement is staged E2E only for the topology audit probe (UID-bracketed). The follow-evidence stats reads (read/promotion eligibility) are NOT UID-bracketed: they are per-pass and by pod name, so a reply from a pod replaced right after the read is used for that pass. The flared-side local read guard (follow_allows_local_read) and the pass-by-pass re-evaluation bound the effect; a UID bracket there is a possible follow-up, not done. ADDRESSED 2026-10-02 (CI pending) without per-read UID calls: follow-evidence replies carry the flared process boot id; a reply whose process differs from the previous pass is Unknown for that pass (FollowEvidence.markProcessChanges). A replacement within one pass (between the read and the commit) is still not detected.

SAF-09 scope (2026-10-02): the durable authority is the operator's own persisted node map. If that ConfigMap is deleted or restored from an older copy, a new leader again starts from the Lease count alone; the check/send race of a deposed leader inside one pass (already a residual) is unchanged; per-node applied generation is observed by the topology audit, not persisted.

2026-10-05 (SAF-09, user priority: tell failure, invalid content, loss and first build apart before any automatic restore): every startup failure used to 'start fresh' — an API error or a missing ConfigMap both logged 'no persisted state found, starting fresh', and a map that did not parse was loaded leniently (bad lines dropped, missing version = 0). Now NodeMapRecovery.decide: valid → load; read failed → retry 12 × 5 s, then exit 2 (pod restarts); invalid → CRITICAL, exit 3; missing/empty + no history → first build; missing/empty + history → CRITICAL, exit 3; evidence unreadable → retry. History = a Lease annotation flare.gree.net/node-map-persisted (written once per process after the first successful persist) or any flared pod reporting a node map version or data. FLARE_NODE_MAP_RESET=1 deliberately accepts a fresh start for the halt cases, never for a failed read (RUNBOOK #node-map-lost). While the operator is halted, flared keeps serving with its last map. Not covered: automatic reconstruction of a lost map; per-node applied generation persisted; a Lease AND ConfigMap lost while every pod restarted reads as a first build. CI pending.

2026-10-05 review round 2 (implemented, NOT CI-verified): the first-build approval is consumed independently of the Lease marker and retried on every persist until it is READ BACK as absent; a removal that does not take logs CRITICAL each persist. RUNBOOK #node-map-lost documents the approval command, its one-shot rule and its UID binding.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37276016227 on 87495a0), classified as FUNCTIONAL — a regression introduced by the SAF-09 Unknown rework and caught by CI: every leg's shared setup installs the chart's operator (namespace flare-system, cluster 'default') with NO FlareCluster and NO flared pods and waits for it to be Ready. With the map missing, the CR read failed (NotFound) and the expected pod count was unknown, so the operator retried, exited and was never Ready; setup timed out in all 8 legs. Before the rework it started fresh. Fix: a FlareCluster confirmed ABSENT (NotFound, not a failed read) with NO flared pod at all and the Lease read without a marker is proven empty (nothing exists to lose); a missing CR with pods stays unknown. The CR, Lease and pod-list read errors are now logged instead of discarded (the failing run did not show the kubectl error).

2026-10-05 review round 3: 'no CR and no pods = nothing to lose' was WRONG (cfb7f02) — PVCs with old data can outlive the CR and the pods, and the Lease marker can be gone too. Replaced (implemented, NOT CI-verified) by separating operator RUNNING from cluster INITIALISATION: with the FlareCluster confirmed absent (NotFound) the operator keeps its lease, reports Ready and WAITS — no node-map decision, no index, no control; only when the CR exists are the persisted map, the history and the first-build approval examined, under the unchanged rules (a recreated CR over old PVCs has a new UID, so no approval applies). A failed CR read is never absence: the operator stays not-Ready and retries. NodeMapRecovery.history no longer proves anything from a missing CR. Lease-read failure is covered by unit cases only (revoking leases would break leader election in E2E).

2026-10-05 review round 4 (static): the waiting loop updated health only on the first NotFound, so NotFound → API error → NotFound stayed not-Ready; health now follows every observation (an empty-UID reply is not-Ready) and only the log is de-duplicated. Test corrections: the pod-list-failure case had left the Lease marker, so the product correctly halted where the test expected a retry — now split into marker present (expect halt) and marker removed and confirmed (expect retry); the old-PVC case required only equal item counts and did not require the PVCs to survive — now it requires the same PVC UIDs and bound volumes claimed by the recreated pods, and compares all 30 keys and values on both copies.

2026-10-05 review round 5 (test/evidence only): the PVC identities were taken AFTER the deletion; they are now captured while the PVCs hold the data, required non-empty, and compared after the deletion and after the pods are recreated. A GET on the replica can be proxied to the master, so 'both copies match' is recorded only with evidence of a local read (the master's cmd_get unchanged while the replica answered all 30 keys). Status unchanged: implemented, CI pending.

2026-10-05 review round 6 (test only): a failed cmd_get read defaulted to 0, so two failed reads compared equal and passed as 'local'. Now both reads are required, the master's pod UID and flared boot id must be equal before and after the reads (a restart resets the counter), and the master's and the replica's roles and pod UIDs must be equal before and after the reads — a change that reverts in between is NOT detected. Status unchanged: implemented, CI pending.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37278389267 on cfb7f02), classified as HARNESS: SAF-09 tests 20 (map missing → halt), 21 (corrupt → halt) and 22 (configmaps forbidden → retry) PASSED; test 23 (compound: map deleted, Lease marker gone, every flared pod restarting) failed only its readiness assertion — the operator logged 'cannot be told from a loss', did not start fresh and wrote no map, but was observed Ready: the undecided operator retries 12 x 5 s, exits 2 and restarts, and the restarted process is briefly a STANDBY, which is Ready by design (rollouts need it). Readiness is not the safety signal; the tests (and cluster-init test 3, same race) now require that the operator never serves its index (port 12120 sampled), never starts fresh and writes no map. The index server starts only after the node-map decision (Main), so a standby or undecided operator never listens.

2026-10-05 review round 7 (test only, not CI-run): the index-port check counted a failed kubectl/exec, a pod without an IP, or a TIMEOUT as 'not open' — missing observations taken as closure. Now a sample counts as CLOSED only if the operator's health port (8080, listening from process start) answered in the same probe and 12120 did not; anything else is NOT OBSERVED, and the test fails unless at least one closed sample was observed (an open sample fails it at once). Status of the HARNESS classifications for PR run 37278389267 (authority compound test, copy-identity tests 2/4/5): based on the logs cited in their run records (docs/reports/2026-10-05-ci-37278389267-*-job.log); NOT independently reviewed. The copy-identity suite's raised breaker floor makes its pass evidence for copy identity only, NOT for recovery time under the production breaker setting.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37283759673 on 8ada54f; NOT independently reviewed). Compound test 23 PASSED, with an observed closed 12120 sample, so it is now positive evidence for the SAF-09 compound path. cluster-init: test 26 (WAITING, no decision, no map) and test 28 (approved first build) PASSED. Tests 27 and 30 failed only their readiness assertions. Classified as HARNESS, with the log as basis. The E2E operator Deployment (FlareOperator/E2E/Setup.lean operatorDeploymentYaml) has NO readinessProbe, unlike the chart (helm values readinessProbe httpGet /readyz:8080), so pod Ready means only 'container running' and cannot reflect /readyz. The job log shows the operator logged 'FlareCluster cluster-init could not be read (... Forbidden ...); retrying — NOT treated as absent' (report line ~4710), and test 27's other two transitions held. Whether /readyz itself turns 503 on a failed read is therefore UNTESTED by this run, not shown to work. CORRECTION to the PR run 37278389267 note above: its readiness failures were attributed to a restarted operator being a Ready STANDBY by design. That explanation was wrong for the E2E harness, which has no readiness probe at all; the index-port criterion added since is unaffected. Test 29 failed its local-read evidence. The log shows 'the replica's reads were served by the master (cmd_get (some 30) -> (some 60))', with the same master UID and boot id: the replica proxied its GETs (readBalance), so the check correctly refused to count them as the replica's copy. Product outcome: no initialisation or re-assignment was logged and the map restore recovered the keys, but the replica-local comparison is NOT evidenced. Test fixes (not yet run): give the E2E operator the chart's readiness probe, and route reads to the replica (readBalance master 0 / slave 100) during the local-read check.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37290297021 on 804e8d6; NOT independently reviewed). With the chart's readiness probe in the E2E operator Deployment, cluster-init 27 PASSED (NotFound Ready → unreadable not-Ready → NotFound Ready again, no decision) and 29 PASSED with the local-read evidence: reads routed to the replica (readBalance master 0 / slave 100, spec restored), master cmd_get 31 -> 31, the same master UID and boot id, the same replica UID, roles unchanged — the replica's own copy served all 30 keys and values. Test 30 failed only its readiness snapshot ('CR unreadable: reported not-absent=true waited as absent=false ready=true'). Classified as HARNESS, by the code rather than by an observation of /readyz: a process starts as a standby, and a standby is Ready by design (HealthCheck.isReady = !leader || tcpReady). The single sample was taken right after the 'NOT treated as absent' line, while the pod's Ready condition still reflected that standby phase; kubelet marks it NotReady only after the readiness failure threshold (3 x 5 s). Test 27, which waits for the transition, passed. The test now samples /readyz itself every 3 s for 30 s (no 200, at least one 503) and waits up to 60 s for the pod to turn NotReady. /readyz returning 503 in this state is still not observed in CI.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37296281060 on ac49d67; NOT independently reviewed). cluster-init 30 PASSED with /readyz sampled directly: with the FlareCluster unreadable, '/readyz over 30 s: 200 x0, 503 x10, not observed x0; pod NotReady within 60 s=true'. This is the direct observation that the earlier HARNESS classification (37290297021: a single pod-Ready sample still showing the standby phase) lacked. cluster-init 29 FAILED on its PRECONDITION ('TIMEOUT after 120s waiting for: both copies hold the keys'; items 30, map saved): the replica did not hold the 30 keys within 120 s before the scenario started. The cause is not investigated: no product verdict for test 29 in this run.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37376724850 on ca694e5; NOT independently reviewed). Authority leg green. cluster-init 29 PASSED this time, with replica-local reads (read routing on, master cmd_get 31 -> 31, same master UID and boot id), where 37296281060 had failed its initial-sync precondition. The earlier precondition failure remains UNEXPLAINED: one pass does not explain it. lag-hold test 25 also passed, but this revision does NOT contain the lag-hold fix (616a010), so the pass shows only that the race did not occur this time.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37419299532 on d47fa82; NOT independently reviewed). cluster-init 29 FAILED, differently from before. After the restore, 'the operator loads the restored map and both copies are back' passed: equal item counts. The local-read check then found the replica WITHOUT init_0, served locally (master cmd_get 31 -> 31, same master UID and boot id; read routing on and verified). So the replica's local copy differed from the master's while the counts were equal. UNEXPLAINED: the captured logs do not show whether a repair or a rebuild was running at that moment. One hypothesis, not verified: the recreated CR has no ledger status, so the first-sighting rule (1969c7c) would request a repair from old drop counters during the test. Kept open, with the earlier initial-sync failure (37296281060), as an unexplained cluster-init 29 record.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37426714842 on f082265; NOT independently reviewed). cluster-init 29 FAILED again. The new diagnostics give a timeline: after the map was restored, the operator set the replica to proxy, re-added it ('NodeAdd … Slave P0 (Prepare)'), and it was RESEEDED by snapshot from the master ('snapshot bootstrap complete … swapped in 15184 bytes'), then Prepare->Active. The earlier 'both copies are back' check had passed on EQUAL COUNTS before that rebuild. During the check the replica's local read lacked init_0 (master cmd_get unchanged, same master UID and boot). After it settled, all 30 keys were present on a verified local read. NOT closed. The replica's own role/state/balance and the read-guard inputs were captured AFTER the failed read (slave/active, reconstruction 1/1), not AT it, so whether the replica answered a local read while it was not allowed to (proxy, or Prepare with balance 0, or mid-swap) is UNDETERMINED. Next diagnostic: bracket each local read with the replica's own state. Product questions: why a restored map re-adds a data-bearing replica and reseeds it, and whether a replica in that transition can answer clients locally.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37438962871 on e2fdc27; NOT independently reviewed). cluster-init 29 FAILED with the split test. (1) during recovery: 1 probe round observed; its 30 answers were all misses and none could be attributed (marker matching by key name failed). (2) after the strengthened 'recovery complete' (replica Active slave, ledger empty, reconstruction 1/1): master all 30 equal; replica init_0..7 answered 'miss', 22 others correct. The trace lines matched to those 8 misses are NOT theirs: they show map_version=0, own_state=prepare, while the replica's state captured just before the same GET shows node_map_version=8589934632, Active slave, balance 0. This is the mis-attribution the review pointed out: this revision matched GETs to traces by key name. The replica's balance was 0 at the first GETs, so they were likely forwarded, but how a forwarded read of a key the master holds came back 'miss' is UNDETERMINED here. Possible readings include a failed forward answered as END (flared's default answers an unreadable key as a miss). No classification. The next revision matches by client connection and logs each answer (hit / miss / unavailable + reason). Separate finding: flared's boot id (time<<32 ^ pid<<16 ^ unseeded random()) is not unique across pods started in the same second (the matched line's boot id equals the master's), so it identifies restarts within one pod only.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37445879349 on 100153c; NOT independently reviewed). cluster-init 29 FAILED its PRECONDITION before the scenario: 'both copies hold the keys' timed out after 120 s (items 30, map saved). No recovery-time or post-recovery reads were made, so this run gives NO evidence for R1. The same precondition failure occurred in 37296281060. Its cause is UNDETERMINED: the failure dump shows only the replica's later restart. Not classified as harness.

2026-10-06 (cd1d9b0: PR run 37451914041 full, and manual single-suite 37451911169; NOT independently reviewed). cluster-init 29 PASSED in both, with the production read policy (readUnavailableError=true). (1) during recovery: 2 probe rounds observed in each run (2-3 not observed); all 60 answers correct, 0 wrong local / forwarded / unattributable, 0 masked misses, 0 explicit errors. The replica was again reseeded by snapshot after the map restore, as in the earlier failures. (2) after recovery: all 30 keys correct AND answered from the replica's own copy, master cmd_get unchanged, same processes. R1 is NOT closed. During the probes the replica's balance was 0, so every probe read was forwarded to the master by policy. The scenario of the earlier failures (37419299532, 37426714842: reads routed to the replica, slave 100, while it was being reseeded) did not occur, so H3 (a local answer from an incomplete copy) was not exercised. Next: probe recovery with reads routed to the replicas.

2026-10-07 (b9e0742 = R3 implementation: PR run 37472032699 full, single-suite 37472022352 empty-source and 37472027476 cluster-init, nix-linux 37472032909; NOT independently reviewed). Linux unit tests: 3573 tests, 0 failures, 1 omission; the boot-id test and the 10 R3 decision tests are listed by name as passing. Full run: topology, replication, wal-recovery, failover-data, repair, repair-ledger, breaker-migration and continuous-replication all PASS with R3 (rebuild of the other replicas on every promotion). SAFETY REGRESSION, empty-source 9: the repair of the replica that missed the deletes was DEFERRED by the empty-source rule ('deferred=true'). Within 60 s the ledger was nevertheless empty and the replica had been demoted to proxy, re-added as Prepare, truncated and dumped from the promoted master: 0/400 keys (full run, empty master) and 2/400 (single run, a 2-key master). The demotion did not come through the deferred repair entry. The path is NOT determined: the operator's lines for that window are not in the failure dump (tail only). R3 is the prime suspect (new on this revision). empty-source 2 (previously passing): the legitimately-emptied-master repair was DEFERRED repeatedly ('the current master holds 0 keys and its source epoch 3:… is not the replica's 2:…'); cause not determined. R2 test: the client exec was cut by the harness's 30 s kubectl exec cap (answer after 30004 ms) while the forward was still retrying; it then succeeded after the cut was healed. This is a test bug shown by the log; the failure answer was not observed; a forward to an unreachable master takes MORE than 30 s. R3 acceptance test: precondition failed (copies not converged after test 9); NOT exercised. cluster-init 29: during recovery no answer came from a pod's own copy; after 'recovery complete' (judged from the operator's view) the replica's own map said Prepare (rebuilding again after the master advanced its epoch twice during the map restore) → explicit errors / forwarded answers, no wrong answer. R10: distinct boot ids across the two pods and across the same-name recreation, observed directly (pods started 5 s apart, so not a same-second observation; that case is the unit test).

2026-10-07 (254640b, single-suite runs 37485235664 empty-source / 37485241380 r3-source-change / 37485248060 cluster-init; NOT independently reviewed). R2 test PASSED: with the cut held, a forward to an unreachable master answered SERVER_ERROR after 36103 ms (server: refused, read_unavailable_error), forwarding works, and an absent key is still a miss. The long forward wait is a separate open item. cluster-init PASSED all 5 with the stricter completion condition. empty-source 9 with the window record: the operator only DEFERRED the replica's repair; no demotion, truncate or dump of the replica in the window. The replica lost keys because 396 of the 400 deletes REACHED it: the master's serial forward queue delivered them after the test healed the cut at the first drop (4 drops counted, 4 keys left). The test premise was not produced, so this is not a destroyed copy. The b9e0742 rebuilds (to 0 and 2 keys) remain UNEXPLAINED: those runs had no window record. R3's rebuild request did not fire in this window (non-follow slaves were read every 30 passes). empty-source 2: the target replica was repaired correctly; the ledger kept R3's request for the OTHER replica, whose copy predates the promotion, and the empty-source rule correctly deferred it. This is no safety violation; the replica stays non-eligible while the master is empty (availability). r3-source-change: test bug — 400 x 1 KB at 256 KB/s finished dumping before the wait saw it in progress. Code survey (subagent, not independently verified): of the operator paths that demote a slave to proxy and re-seat it, only replica repair matches test 9; it checks the source only at demotion, not at release/reseat/copy, and accepts any non-zero master count. flared's only guard before truncate/swap is an LSN comparison. Other paths bypass the source check: drain, failover + re-registration, restart boot shift, zone swap, stale map on takeover, space-aware hard_reset, corrupt-DB wipe, interrupted-restore wipe, flush_all to a replica, and WAL catch-up without epoch.

2026-10-07 (3f497b0, single-suite runs 37493280795 empty-source and 37493288883 r3-source-change; NOT independently reviewed). R3 acceptance, forced order produced: the replica activated on the OLD master's copy (log line 130). Then, in one step, it accepted the map naming the new master and its eligibility was withdrawn (lines 141/142). Right after, it reported eligible=0 (revalidating) while its own map said Active slave, balance 100. There were 0 local read decisions between that acceptance and being re-bound. Then: NEEDS REBUILD; the operator logged 'REPLICA REPAIR requested by the replica … R3' → 'demoting … rebuild source holds data' → confirmed → released → re-seated; rebuilt and bound to the new master. The test failed on two TEST issues, shown by the log: (1) the reads during re-validation used 30 keys, and each forward to the unreachable master takes ~36 s; (2) 'rebound' was judged from the binding, which is made at the source check BEFORE activation, so the after-reads met a Prepare replica (correct values, forwarded). Both fixed. The operator log confirms the structure behind hypothesis H1: R3's rebuild request is judged by the source check at DEMOTION time ('rebuild source … holds data'), and the copy happens after release and re-seat, with no re-check. empty-source: test 2 passes. Test 9 failed its first precondition (no other slave still carried evidence of the earlier history) because, with stats read every pass, R3 got that replica rebuilt from the full new master right after the promotion. Consistent with H1's timing dependence; not a proof.

2026-10-07 (R3-D: 94166ba and 610ebb7; NOT independently reviewed). 9bb08db had a regression of my own: the operator's release re-check read the DEMOTED replica's partition (-1) and held every repair forever (45 'release HELD … no Active master' lines; follower rebuilds never ran). Fixed in 94166ba. 94166ba: copy-protection passed in the full run. empty-source test 2 (legitimate empty master) was REFUSED by the new flared protection: the attempt durably dropped the rebuild evidence before the protection read it; tests 3-9 failed their preconditions in a cascade. Fixed in 610ebb7: the copy is judged by its identity captured before the evidence was dropped. 610ebb7: copy-protection PASSES in the full run 37547974017 and the single-suite run 37547972944. checks.procedure: Run flare_unit observation cases: complete/truncated/duplicate stats; older/equal/newer version; missing/changing UID; new Unknown replaces old confirmation. Continuous-replication requires a UID-bound current observation from the production audit. Replacement during probe and startup republish as sole recovery remain unstaged. E2E (2026-10-01, CI pending): topology-authority test 'same-name Pod replacement during the topology probe' holds the probe of the slave after its first UID read (test seam FLARE_TEST_PROBE_BARRIER, 30 s ceiling), force-replaces the pod under the same name, releases, and requires the first audit line for that pod after the release to carry verdict=unknown; then requires a later probe of the new UID to report verdict=current and the topology to be applied.

Drive the production reconcile to a named stop position (committed, version advanced, pre-send lease check not yet made) using the FLARE_TEST_PRESEND_BARRIER seam, and confirm the position was reached by reading the held version the operator writes there. Topology changes are triggered by patching the FlareCluster readBalance spec (non-destructive). Then, for the same held pass: (a) retain the lease and require the release to broadcast that version - the control that proves the pass reaches the send at all; (b) hand the lease to another identity and require a fence log naming that version with no broadcast, then require the container restart count to move (losing the lease is designed to end the process), the restarted process to log lease acquisition, and the topology to be applied - exactly one Active master, every node Active, each flared's own `stats nodes` naming that master; (c) delete the lease and require the read-failure branch with no broadcast, then a later pass of the SAME process that publishes and names the suppressed version, and the applied topology. A receiver whose version does not move is not accepted as evidence on its own: a crash, a timeout or an exit before the branch look the same. Separately, push a mutated map at a stale version from inside the cluster and require flared both to keep its map and to log the rejection. Every test releases the barrier and restores authority before judging.

E2E topology-authority, test 'startup republish alone': hold one committed pass at the pre-send barrier (version H, a read-balance weight change), then replace the operator with a Deployment rollout that sets FLARE_TEST_TOPOLOGY_AUDIT_OFF=1 while the pass is held, so the map is persisted and never sent. Require: the operator pod was replaced; the fresh process logs the audit seam and no [TopologyAudit] probe; it resumed from the persisted map at a version >= H; its FIRST send's logged trigger record is pending-only (versionMoved=false, repairHeld=0, activeNotReady=0, pending=vX) and the matching broadcast line is (vX -> vX); every flared pod then reports node_map_version X AND the operator's committed slave balance in its own `stats nodes`, which must differ from what the pods showed before. Unit: BroadcastTriggers.any / pendingOnly / label cases in flare_unit.

SAF-09 durable authority. Proofs startupVersion_gt_resumed (a new leader's first version is above every persisted version) and startupGeneration_ge_lease; flare_unit cases for a recreated Lease (transitions 0), a Lease count above the persisted generation, equal counts, a fresh cluster, and persistedCovers. E2E topology-authority test 'SAF-09: the Lease is deleted and the operator replaced': read the persisted node-map version, delete the Lease and the operator pod, require the new leader's logged generation to exceed the persisted generation although its Lease count restarted, then require a topology change to reach every pod at a version at or above generation*2^32 and the topology to be applied. The persist fence (no send above the durable record; a failed write suppresses the send and keeps it pending) is exercised by every send; its failure branch is unit-level only.

SAF-09 startup node map. flare_unit checkNodeMapRecovery (19 cases): a valid map loads; a failed read retries and is never treated as absent, even with FLARE_NODE_MAP_RESET; missing or empty + no history = first build; missing or empty + history (Lease marker or a flared pod with a node map version or data) = halt; unreadable evidence = retry; six kinds of invalid content halt instead of loading partially; only (NotFound) counts as absent; a not-Ready unreadable pod gives no evidence (first build: flared waits for the operator), a Ready unreadable pod leaves it unknown. E2E topology-authority (3 tests): with the operator stopped, (1) the ConfigMap deleted → on start it halts with the CRITICAL line, never starts fresh or becomes Ready, flared keeps its map version and serves a set; restoring the ConfigMap brings it back; (2) the map corrupted → halt, restore → back; (3) configmaps forbidden by RBAC → it retries and does not start fresh, then loads the existing map once readable.

SAF-09 operator vs cluster initialisation. E2E cluster-init (1p x 2r PVC, operator deployed before its cluster): (1) no FlareCluster and no pods — the operator is Ready and WAITING, makes no node-map decision and persists no node map; (1b) NotFound (Ready) → the FlareCluster unreadable by RBAC (not Ready, a failed read logged, not absent) → NotFound again (Ready again), still no decision; (2) the CR then appears with a first-build approval — the operator examines it, builds it, the cluster serves writes, and the approval is consumed; (3) the CR, StatefulSet, map and Lease marker are deleted while the PVCs stay, then the CR and StatefulSet are recreated WITHOUT approval — the operator must never start fresh, never become Ready and write no map; each PVC's name, UID and bound volume are captured while it still holds the data (both must be non-empty) and must be unchanged after the deletion and claimed by the recreated pods; after restoring the map all 30 keys and values read back through the master and through the replica, and the replica's reads count as its LOCAL copy only if the master's cmd_get was read before AND after and did not move, the master's pod UID and flared boot id are equal before and after the reads, and the master's and the replica's roles and pod UIDs are equal before and after the reads (a change that reverts in between is not detected); (4) with flareclusters unreadable (RBAC) the operator must report a failed read, not WAIT as if absent, and not become Ready; with the map missing and pods unreadable: with the Lease marker present it must HALT (the cluster ran before), with the marker removed (confirmed) it must retry as undecidable — never fresh either way.

constraint.text: A replica with missed writes remains repair-pending until reconstruction completes and missing data is recovered.

controls.title: Repair dropped replica writes
scenarios: Drops during normal service, a drop while the gate is held, an unresolved destination, operator restart with the ledger persisted, a master counter reset, drops arriving after a repair's reconstruction began, a failed ledger save, and a corrupt/unreadable ledger at start.

A drop whose destination is a WAL-mode follower (SAF-10): the ledger entry is HELD under the follower's ownership (no demotion, no rebuild), CLOSED when the follower's contiguous applied position reaches the master's position at request time in the SAME source epoch, HANDED OVER to the rebuild path only if the follower explicitly stops owning; an unreadable follower state (stats fetch failure) keeps the hold.
assumptions: Drop counters describe a source/destination incarnation (a counter that went down is a restart whose count is entirely new drops). flared keeps one completion RECORD per process — a random boot id, the latest reconstruction's id and state, and the id and source of the last success — so a completion can be tied to a process and a source; cumulative started/completed counters cannot (a failed handler leaves them unequal forever, a restart may reproduce their values).
residual_risks: A repair rebuilds the whole partition; there is no per-key repair.

Drops attributed after the reseat are requeued on completion; a drop in the LAST stretch of a live reconstruction is pinned by flare_unit, not staged end to end (a tiny dataset reconstructs within one pass).
The completion record is read over the stats channel; an unreadable record holds the entry (fail closed) rather than completing it.
A destination that became a MASTER while under repair is VOIDED, not repaired.
A write that keeps failing until a restart loses the unsaved delta; the window is one pass of retries, extended by however long the cause (e.g. a revoked RBAC grant) persists.

The operator announces an unsaved ledger ('marked unsaved and will retry every pass — an operator restart before that lands would lose ...') but a landing through the normal per-pass persist is silent, so the log does not show when that exposure ended (only the retry path logs 'persisted on retry'). Observability gap; follow-up proposed.

RBAC grant propagation: one local observation (2026-09-13) of ~131s before an impersonated `can-i` flipped after a restore; CI runs 6 and 8 saw the grant effective for the operator's own SA within seconds (in-pod probe). Earlier attributions of >2 minutes to the operator's path were harness artefacts (see the round-8 review note).

Until eb2ba17 the drop observation required the REPLICA's stats read to succeed as well as the master's, so an unreadable replica hid the master's drop counter for its partition (found by the SAF-10d stats-fetch-failure scenario, run 4). Fixed: the observation needs the master's reply only. E2E confirmation pending (run 5).

REGRESSION (found by rerunning replica-repair on tch after SAF-10c, fixed 2379cff): FollowReading treated a complete stats reply WITHOUT follower keys as unreadable, so every drop on a non-RocksDB replica was held as 'follower state unknown' and never repaired. Unknown now means a failed or truncated read only. The rerun of the non-WAL suites on the fix is pending.

2026-10-02 (CI 36882921953), classified as HARNESS: replica-repair test 4 failed 'completion was logged but no demotion was observed'. The operator log shows the new process demoted, saw the demotion confirmed and completed, in that order. The completion wait began only after the new process had finished the whole repair, about 60 s earlier than in the passing runs (55-65 s). Cause in the harness: `kubectl rollout status` returns while the old operator pod is still terminating, so the 'restores the HELD request' check passed on the OLD pod's log; the completion wait then read a 2000-line tail. Tests 5 and 6 failed on preconditions left by 4. Fix: every operator rollout in the suite waits until the previous pod is gone, and the completion wait reads the full log. Re-run 36887321961: replica-repair 15/15; the previous operator pod outlived `rollout status` by 35 s at every rollout, and the HELD-restore check now takes 15 s on the new pod instead of passing at once on the old one.

2026-10-02 (PR run 37007523101 on b01ff4d), classified as FUNCTIONAL (operator), fixed in 713bf8c: after the kill -9 in continuous-replication test 14 the replica restarted on its PVC, followed and matched the master (items 356/356), but the ledger entry (an ordinary request, no hold) never closed within 300 s. The replica's flared log shows why: its reconstruction finished, then activate_node was refused 30 times as 'node state: transition 0→0 not allowed', the attempt was failed and the whole reconstruction restarted, up to attempt 7. The operator already had the node Active: either its PREPARE-REPAIR activated it from sync evidence while flared was finishing, or an earlier activate was applied and its reply lost. Since the reconstruction never returned success, the 'reconstruction newer than at reseat SUCCEEDED' completion the entry waits for never came. Test 15 (planned promotion, 'did not advance the source epoch') then promoted the same node while it was still inside that retry loop, so it is a consequence of the same defect. Fix: Reconciler.reconcileStep acknowledges an Active/Ready report for a node that is already Active without changing the state (IDEMPOTENT RE-ACTIVATION); Down and other states are still refused. flare_unit checkReactivation (4 cases) and GeneralSafety's CLE proof cover it; re-run PASS: PR run 37014778271 (merge revision 35818b4 of 713bf8c), all 8 legs green, continuous-replication tests 14 and 15 pass and the 'not allowed' refusal does not occur in the leg's log. One passing run does not show the race is gone, only that the fixed path works. The 9 earlier PR runs passed this test, so the race is intermittent.

2026-10-05 SAF-08: a replica-repair demotion rebuilds the copy from the partition's CURRENT master, which may not be the one that counted the drops and was never checked; it is now deferred (request kept) unless that master is known to hold data, and applied with an atomic regEpoch re-check (a TCP re-registration between read and write used to be overwritten).

2026-10-06 PRODUCT GAP found by empty-source test 2 (PR runs 37296281060 and 37376724850; NOT independently reviewed). The repair ledger takes its FIRST observation of the master's proxy_write_dropped counters as BASELINE ('replica repair ledger initialized from … recorded as baseline, none attributed', ReplicaRepair.classify: none + not initialized = baseline). Observations happen once per stats probe slot (FLARE_STATS_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS, default 300 s). So drops that happen before the first probe after a fresh ledger are never attributed and never repaired: on a new cluster, or when the ledger status was lost. In 37376724850, 400 deletes were sent while the replica's forwards were cut; 396 were delivered later by forwarding retries, 4 exhausted their retries and were counted as dropped, and the ledger was initialized AFTER that count. The replica kept 4 deleted keys, the ledger stayed empty and nothing deferred — the earlier 'unexplained 2 items / empty ledger' (37296281060) fits the same mechanism. A ledger that was already initialized attributes a newly seen master's counters (classify: none + initialized = increased), so promotions are not affected. Proposal for review (not implemented): on first sighting, a non-zero counter becomes a repair request instead of a baseline (cost: a possibly unnecessary rebuild after an operator upgrade or lost status), or the operator probes at once at start instead of waiting a slot. empty-source test 2 now requires the ledger to be initialized before its fault, so it tests the repair decision separately from this gap.

2026-10-06 (implemented in 1969c7c, CI pending; NOT reviewed). Decision: a non-zero count at the ledger's FIRST observation is kept as a POSSIBLY UNREPAIRED request, not a baseline. Probing at start was rejected: it only narrows the window. No immediate demotion: the request takes the same follower-ownership and source/copy gates as any request. Counters are keyed by the master's flared boot id when known: a restarted master's count is new, the old process's keys are dropped, and the same cumulative value is never requested twice. After an upgrade the boot-less keys are replaced, so historical drops are requested once (a possibly unnecessary rebuild, accepted). E2E repair-ledger (own leg): drops before the first observation (precondition: ledger not yet initialized at the fault) are requested and repaired; no second request across an operator restart; a restarted master's new drops are attributed in full exactly once. Status-save failure and the ledger surviving a restart are covered by replica-repair tests 4-5 (same persistence path); a status-save failure DURING a first-sighting request is not separately staged.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37407630865 on bf096f0; NOT independently reviewed). repair-ledger PASSED all three tests. (1) A drop before the ledger's first observation was requested ('first-observation request=true') and the replica repaired (40 = 40 items). (2) After an operator restart, no request line appeared in the restarted operator (0) and the ledger stayed empty. (3) After the master's flared restarted (boot 7693392365839074663 -> 7693392408788747623), 30 writes with forwards cut produced 2 drops; they were requested once and repaired (70 = 70).

2026-10-06 (PR run 37419299532 on d47fa82; NOT independently reviewed). repair-ledger test 1 FAILED its precondition: 'the ledger was already initialized before the fault (window missed)'. The test waited for the stats probe slot, whose phase relative to the operator's start is arbitrary (slot = monotonic time / interval), so the first observation can come before the fault. This is a test design race, not a product failure; it passed in 37407630865. The test is now deterministic: stop the operator, cause the drops, remove the persisted ledger (as on a new cluster or lost status), then start the operator, whose FIRST observation already sees the drops.
controls.call_path: queue_proxy_write records destination drops -> stats proxy_write_dropped[dest] -> Main observe (only while the ledger is AVAILABLE; a partially corrupt ledger is unavailable, not smaller) -> ReplicaRepair ledger (persisted; dirty writes retried) -> demote to Proxy held out of assignment -> node confirms (boot id, current id, drops at reseat recorded) -> FSM re-seats Slave/Prepare -> flared reconstructs -> complete when the LATEST reconstruction SUCCEEDED from the current master and is newer than the reseat one in the same process, or in a new process (boot id changed); late drops requeued.

checks.procedure: Against real flared: cut master->slave traffic on the node (iptables REJECT), write keys, confirm the master counts proxy_write_dropped and the slave's LOCAL curr_items falls behind. Heal, then require REQUEST (log, status entry, metric), DEMOTE and HOLD, the node's CONFIRMATION, RE-SEAT and a reconstruction that began after it and finished (flared started/completed), COMPLETE, empty ledger, slave curr_items reaching the master's, no further drop. SAF-05: with FLARE_RESYNC_ON_DROP=0 the drop is HELD, survives an operator restart, and is repaired once the gate opens. Ledger faults: with the operator's write to flareclusters/status revoked, a new request is marked UNSAVED, retried each pass, absent from status, lands when the permission returns, and survives a restart; with status.replicaRepairs corrupted, the restarted operator reports the ledger UNAVAILABLE (never starts fresh), accounts no drop meanwhile, and once the ledger is repaired requests and recovers the drop seen during the outage.

flare_unit pins the ledger decisions on flared's completion record: release records boot id/current id/drops; a re-announced Active, a newer reconstruction still running, a newer one that FAILED, or a success from another source is NOT completion; a success newer than the reseat one completes; failure-then-success completes; a RESTART with identical counters completes because the boot id differs; a restart still running does not; late drops requeue exactly the increment; a partially corrupt ledger (missing masterKey, malformed counter, unknown phase, one bad among good) fails as a whole.

RocksDB, repl-identity-forward and repl-follow-enabled on for every node, replica read balance 0: verify both flags on all pods; write and see the replica apply forwarded changes through the common rule while following; cut master<->replica (iptables REJECT both ways), create/update/delete on the master until proxy_write_dropped is counted and stops increasing, STOP writing; heal and require the replica to resume from its applied_lsn to the master's position at the cut while following, item counts equal and the updated/created keys read correctly by DIRECT replica reads, reconstruction_started unchanged and the pod uid unchanged; require the ledger entry to be logged HELD as owned by the follower and then CLOSED by continuous replication with no demotion and no hand-over, status.replicaRepairs empty. Separately, with the operator's pods/exec revoked (inert resource name, original list restored after), a new drop is HELD as 'follower state unknown (stats unreadable)', never demoted while blind, and CLOSED once the probe returns.

E2E repair-ledger (own leg, FLARE_STATS_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS 180000): (1) writes dropped BEFORE the ledger's first observation (precondition: no 'ledger initialized' line at the fault) are requested as 'first observation' and the replica is repaired; (2) the same cumulative counter is not requested again across an operator restart; (3) after the master's flared restarts (new boot id, counter reset) its new drops are requested exactly once and repaired. Unit: flare_unit checkLedgerObserve / checkObserve.

constraint.text: Normal promotion and Prepare activation require a completed usable copy associated with the current source.

controls.title: Require valid synchronization evidence
scenarios: A Prepare slave whose activation was lost to an index-leader handover (reconstruction finished, operator still sees Prepare); a node with a PAST success that is now re-reconstructing (in flight); a RocksDB reply missing lineage or cursor (truncated); a zero cursor; a mismatched lineage; a cursor ahead of the head; a master or lineage change mid-observation; a fresh process.

SAF-10c: a WAL-mode follower as promotion candidate — proven current (following the master's current epoch, fresh by the node's own clock, lag within the promotion bound) is preferred; disconnected/stale/lagging/unreadable is unproven (no planned promotion, last resort for failover, logged NOT LOSS-FREE); needs_rebuild/initial_sync/idle/another epoch is unfit (never promoted by the FSM paths).
assumptions: flared exposes a per-process completion record in stats, read as ONE locked snapshot: reconstruction_boot_id (random per process), reconstruction_current_id/_state (latest handler), reconstruction_last_success_id/_source. Every notification carries the id the handler was given at begin(), so an older handler finishing after a newer one started cannot record the newer id as succeeded; last_success only advances and only the current handler's notification changes current_state. Activation requires the LATEST reconstruction to have succeeded from the current master. On RocksDB a completed reconstruction seeds a nonzero cursor and rocksdb_master_id identifies the source; the backend is told from a COMPLETE master reply.
residual_risks: Covers Prepare ACTIVATION by the repair path only; promotion still trusts the Active designation (SAF-08).

On a backend that reports no lineage/cursor (complete reply, no rocksdb_ keys) a completion with none in flight is accepted; the vacuous-activation guard in reconcileStep still requires an Active master to have synced from.
The prepare-evidence E2E runs on the tch backend, so the RocksDB lineage/cursor requirement is pinned by flare_unit, not staged end to end.

SAF-10c: failover with the master gone cannot prove currency (asynchronous replication); the FSM still promotes for availability and only logs that it is not loss-free. The TCP-side zombie-master guard (Reconciler.findActiveSlaveForPartition) does not consult follower evidence. Audit follow-up withholds never-read replicas until their mode is established (unit tested); independent stale-map routing and the amended read-value E2E are not yet executed. Prior E2E evidence does not validate this new local read guard.

The planned-promotion E2E (CHECK-04-follow) failed once on CI (run 36748059941) because the master was deleted inside a freshly restarted operator's 120 s startup grace period, during which drain and dead detection are skipped; no promotion of any kind happened and the recreated master re-registered. Harness precondition (fixed: the test waits for the operator to be older than 150 s); the operational consequence stands — a planned master removal within two minutes of an operator (re)start is not drained.

The planned-promotion E2E has never found the operator's 'graceful drain' line on CI even when it passes; it establishes that the proven follower is promoted and the epoch advances, not that the drain path (rather than failover after the preStop window) carried it. The drain-path exclusion of unproven followers therefore remains unit-pinned only.

2026-10-01 diagnosis of the drain caveat (CI pending): the startup grace is 24 reconcile CYCLES, not 120 s; with 2-3 s passes in the continuous-replication suite they last ~190 s, so the test's wait for a 150 s-old operator still deleted the master inside the grace, where the operator skips drain and dead detection. The follower was then promoted ~35 s later by dead-node failover once grace ended, which is why no drain line ever appeared (the terminating-pod suite, with fewer probes, does observe the drain). The test now waits for the operator's own 'grace period: 0 cycles remaining' line and REQUIRES the drain line; earlier PASS records on CHECK-04-follow proved promotion of the proven follower and the epoch advance, not the drain path. Separately: a grace measured in cycles stretches with slow passes; whether it should be wall-clock is a design question.

FINDING 2026-10-01 (CI 36841064685, functional): with the grace wait fixed, the drain ran but its guard REFUSED the proven follower ('NO promotable successor'); the follower was promoted ~35 s later by dead-node failover. Cause: the follow-evidence probe read the master's head only from pods that were Ready AND not Terminating, and during a drain the master is Terminating by definition, so no follower could be proven current and every planned promotion in follow mode was refused. Production impact: a planned master restart in follow mode did not hand off during preStop; writes in the preStop window and the gap until failover were served by a master about to exit. FIX (CI pending): the master's head is read from any Ready pod, Terminating included; the planned-promotion E2E now fails when the guard refuses.

DECISION 2026-10-02 (user): the startup grace is wall-clock (FLARE_STARTUP_GRACE_SECONDS, default 120 s) instead of 24 reconcile cycles; the operator logs 'grace period over after Ns' once, and the planned-promotion E2E waits for that line.

FINDING 2026-10-02 (CI 36909742559, test premise; behaviour by design but now stated): with the breaker floor, the 1p x 2r failover happened (the follower was promoted), but WITHOUT the NOT LOSS-FREE line while 48 items were lost. The cut is one-way (master->replica forwards), so the follower kept polling the master's WAL position and was within the promotion bound (FLARE_FOLLOW_PROMOTE_LAG, default 100 positions) and counted as proven; the force-deleted master appears Terminating, so the drain path promoted it. Guarantee as implemented: no warning => loss <= the promotion bound; a promotion within the bound loses up to that many positions silently. The test now asserts exactly that (warning, or gap <= 100) and prints the promotion path; the suite gained a failure dump.

2026-10-02 (user decision: refuse automatic promotion of a follower that is too far behind): FollowEvidence.Bounds.failoverMaxLag (FLARE_FOLLOW_FAILOVER_MAX_LAG, default 100000 positions) makes a follower whose last observed backlog (source position minus applied position) exceeds it UNFIT, so failover does not promote it and waits for the old master to return with its data; the last-resort refill can still seat it when it is the only data-bearing copy (logged NOT LOSS-FREE). Three unit cases. CI pending; not yet exercised end to end.
controls.call_path: flared finishes reconstruction and calls activate_node; if the operator returned OK but did not persist it (leader handover) the node stays Prepare in the operator map. Main 4c builds a per-node episode, reads flared stats (reconstruction_completed, rocksdb_master_id, cursor + master head), SyncEvidence.judge requires a completed reconstruction bound to the current master's lineage with a sane cursor and unchanged source, and a positive verdict re-derives Prepare->Active through Reconciler.reconcileStep.

checks.procedure: Stage the lost activation with the TCP-server seam (FLARE_TEST_DROP_NODE_STATE) so the slave's reconstruction completes while the operator keeps it Prepare; assert the seam dropped an event and reconstruction_completed >= 1 (persistent signals), then that the repair activates on the NAMED evidence (N reconstruction(s) completed, none in flight; backend classification) and not on a cursor distance, applied through reconcileStep.

flare_unit pins SyncEvidence.judge on the completion record: latest running / failed / aborted refused; success from another source refused; #0 refused; the first review's LSN-0 input refused (cursor not seeded); lineage mismatch, cursor ahead, missing RocksDB lineage/cursor, and an incomplete master reply refused; failure-then-success (#2 succeeded after #1 failed) and abort-then-success ACCEPTED; a new process's own success accepted; a far-behind seeded cursor accepted; non-RocksDB accepted on the record; a source change refused until a success from the new master with matching lineage.

cutter test_stats_reconstruction pins the record's id binding: A begins #1, B begins #2, A succeeds -> current #2 still running, last_success #1 (not #2); a late success of an older handler does not regress a newer one; an older handler's failure or abort does not change the current state; a current failure after an earlier success leaves last_success != current so a controller must not activate.

flare_unit pins FollowEvidence.judge (unreadable → unknown; mode off → notInMode; not following, another epoch, stale observation, lag over the bound, applied ahead of the head → ineligible; unreadable master → unknown; lag at the bound eligible; read vs promotion bounds), unfitReason, classify (ranked highest-applied first; unproven vs unfit; withheld reads; mode memory; remembered-in-mode unreadable/not-probed → unproven and withheld, never unfit; no master reading → nothing proven), the probe policy, shapePromotionCandidates (unfit removed, ranked first, unproven last, nodeMap untouched, findActiveSuccessor sees the order, all-excluded leaves no successor), withholdReads (slave 0, master/Down/unlisted untouched, keys preserved) and the masterless refill's exclusion. E2E (2026-10-01, CI pending): continuous-replication test 'operator restart while the replica's stats cannot be read' sets spec slave=50 and waits for the following replica to be served, revokes the operator's pods/exec on the replica, replaces the operator pod, and requires the fresh process to withhold the replica (committed balance 0), the follower to keep following, the master unchanged and no demotion; after pods/exec is restored the replica must be served at 50 again with no reconstruction and the same pod UID. E2E (2026-10-01, CI pending), non-follow-mode recovery: read-balance test 'operator restart in a cluster without follow mode' replaces the operator with spec slave=100 and a standby, and requires the fresh operator to log its stats probe, every regular slave to be back at 100 and the standby at 0 within 120 s, and no follow-eligibility decision in that cluster. SAF-08 (2026-10-02): flare_unit cases for markProcessChanges — first sighting not marked; a changed boot id makes an eligible follower Unknown (withheld, unproven, not unfit); the second consistent reading restores eligibility; unprobed nodes keep their boot id; a node out of the mode keeps the legacy policy.

Invoke production pre_proxy_read with a stale positive slave balance: caught-up permits local read, disconnected and lagging attempt master enqueue rather than local read, recovery permits local read again, wrong source refuses local read. A deliberately unavailable transport proves fail-closed branch selection, not successful network delivery; real socket E2E remains required.

E2E continuous-replication tests 8 and 11: with spec.readBalance.slave=50 the following replica is served (balance 50), withheld to 0 while cut, restored after healing; the master pod is deleted, the follower is promoted, its source epoch advances, the returning ex-master rebuilds and follows the new epoch. Planned-promotion (drain) exclusion and the NOT LOSS-FREE line for an unproven promotion are not yet staged. Lagged successor (2026-10-02, CI pending): continuous-replication-limits test 'lagged successor' cuts the follower, writes 50 keys on the master, force-deletes the master, and requires failover to promote the follower with the PROMOTION NOT LOSS-FREE line naming it, records the item gap (the asynchronous RPO), and requires the returning ex-master to rejoin as a follower of the new master.

constraint.text: Delete only a revalidated target when independent current evidence supports the surviving copy.

controls.title: Protect copies before deleting Pods
scenarios: An empty-master candidate whose stats are missing/truncated (must not read as empty); a successor demoted by a resync between observation and delete; the target pod replaced under the same name; the operator losing its lease before the delete.

SAF-10c: the surviving copy is a WAL-mode follower — the delete proceeds only if, from the same fresh stats read at revalidation, it is following the master's current epoch, fresh, and within the promotion lag bound; unknown or ineligible refuses.
assumptions: curr_items is local storage; a stats reply with no well-formed curr_items line carries no information. A StatefulSet reuses a pod NAME for a replacement, so identity is the pod UID. The leader lease is the operator's authority to act.
residual_risks: Graceful deletion still does not guarantee a successful handoff; the drain guard protects a master with no promotable successor.
The successor/lease revalidation and the delete are not one atomic step; the pod-identity hole is closed by the API precondition, a successor demoted in the instant after the gate remains a window.

The direct-API delete is bounded (connect 3s, total 10s, outer wall 20s + 5s kill grace, ~25s worst case). A timeout or transport failure is an UNKNOWN deletion outcome — the API may have accepted the delete and only the reply was lost — and is reported as such; the caller keeps the streak and re-observes the pod on the next probe rather than assuming 'not deleted' or retrying blindly.

A live empty master with a data-bearing successor and an interposed change is not staged end to end; the gate is unit-pinned, the precondition and the deadline are staged by E2E against a replaced pod and a black-hole server.

SAF-10c: the survivor's currency is judged from one fresh reading at revalidation; a follower that disconnects in the instant after the gate remains a window (same shape as the successor-demotion window). Unit-pinned only.

Until d9d1285 storage_rocksdb::open seeded curr_items from rocksdb.estimate-num-keys, which does not count keys recovered from the WAL: after a crash the count under-reported by the unflushed tail (SAF-10d run 9: 52 keys present, not counted), so a count-based comparison could read intact data as loss — or, on a small DB, an intact master as empty. Fixed by an exact scan at open; unit-pinned (test_reopen_counts_wal_only_keys_exactly) and observed in E2E run 10.
controls.call_path: Main 4d probes master/slave curr_items -> parseCurrItems -> emptyMasterVerdict -> streak >= 3 -> REVALIDATE: pod UID, fresh stats, UID again, live map AFTER the stats, leader lease -> deleteGate -> Bridge.deletePodWithUidPrecondition: DELETE with DeleteOptions.preconditions.uid = the observed UID, refused by the apiserver (409) if another pod holds the name -> drain path.

checks.procedure: Malformed/empty/truncated stats must not delete a master; act only on a confirmed empty master with a confirmed data-bearing successor; revalidate stats, then the live map, then the lease, with the target UID stable across the observation; the delete carries the observed UID as an API-side precondition. E2E (replica-repair test 7) runs the operator's exact delete command inside the operator pod: accepted (200/202) for the matching UID, and refused (409) for a same-name replacement with another UID, which survives. Deadline (test 12): the same command aimed at a server that ACCEPTS the connection — proved server-side by the bytes the black hole received — and never answers ends by curl's TIMEOUT (exit 28) within the deadline; a refused connection (exit 7) does not pass this test, and the caller is told the outcome is unknown, not 'not deleted'.

flare_unit pins parseCurrItems (blank/missing/non-numeric are unknown, genuine 0 is known 0), emptyMasterVerdict (act only on known-0 + known data-bearing), successorStillValid (invalid when not data-bearing, demoted to Proxy, or the target is no longer an Active master), and deleteGate (refuses when the OPERATOR lost its lease, the pod UID changed, the successor is invalid on the post-read map, or the fresh verdict is skip).
flare_unit pins deleteGate's survivorFollowOk: an unproven surviving follower refuses the delete with a reason naming continuous replication; the survive purpose uses the promotion bound.
