constraint.text: Refill missing masters under an explicit emergency policy, with partial-copy promotion distinguished from normal successor promotion.

controls.title: Make emergency refill tradeoffs explicit
scenarios: All copies restart; only a Prepare copy remains; probes fail or return empty data.

The master dies while its only follower is connected but further behind than the failover lag bound (or declared its copy unusable): the follower is not seated while the ex-master is away; the partition waits, bounded, for the ex-master's copy; an ex-master back without data, or an exhausted wait, seats the follower as an explicit NOT LOSS-FREE last resort.
assumptions: Availability may deliberately be chosen over completeness; data-bearing means nonzero count, not a complete or newest copy.
residual_risks: Active candidates lack a data check; absent data-bearing observations fall back; Prepare partial copies can become authoritative.

pvc-data-survival's total-P0-loss test (CHECK-06) failed once on CI (run 36707861123) with 'DATA LOSS: 10 missing' that was a HARNESS precondition fault: the recovery wait was satisfied by stale StatefulSet/operator state 15 s after a force delete, and the readback hit a booting pod (first ten GETs in order missed; P0 count 49 = passing run). The wait now requires replaced pod UIDs, Ready replicas and a stats-answering master (report 2026-09-30-sustained-after-more-fix.md). The failure is kept; the fix is re-executed by the next PR run.

2026-10-02 (CI 36909742559), classified as HARNESS: 'DATA LOSS: 5 missing' in pvc-data-survival test 2 was not a loss. flared on the restarted reading pod logged 'partition error (key=pvc_0..pvc_4) -> continue processing (pretending not found)': it had not received its partition map yet when the test read 11 s after the restart. The test now re-reads only missing keys for up to 30 s (a real loss stays missing; a mismatch is never retried). The same behaviour is what flared's read-unavailable-error option turns into SERVER_ERROR.

2026-10-03, found by reading the code, then reproduced in a pure check (no CI run): the failover lag bound (FLARE_FOLLOW_FAILOVER_MAX_LAG, added after the scale evaluation lost ~1.83M acknowledged writes) only kept the unfit follower out of handleFailoverWithPromotion. In the same pass promoteMasterlessPartition's data-bearing last resort crowned it, and that crowning logged no NOT LOSS-FREE line, so the bound protected nothing. A second gap: dataBearingPodKeys read only Ready pods, and a returning ex-master is NotReady in Prepare, so it would have looked empty. Fix: the refill holds an unfit follower while the partition's ex-master is away, up to FLARE_FOLLOW_FAILOVER_WAIT_SECONDS (default 300, counted from the first masterless pass; 0 = old behaviour); an ex-master back without data ends the hold at once; both the hold (CRITICAL) and a last-resort crowning (NOT LOSS-FREE) are logged; ex-masters (lastMasterOf holders) are read for data even while NotReady. Trade-off: the partition takes no writes during the hold. The hold covers only a follower that KNOWS its backlog: a follower cut off from its master never sees the head advance, so it is unproven, not unfit, and is still promoted (async loss, accepted as A0). E2E continuous-replication-lag-hold pending CI.

2026-10-03 (PR run 37025254148 on 44a2402), the first lag-hold E2E FAILED. The behaviour held: the operator judged the follower unfit (applied 4 of source 144), the master was force-deleted, the follower was never promoted, and the ex-master was master again. But the hold never ran: the StatefulSet's replacement pod re-registered before dead detection and the refill re-seated it in the same pass (tier 3), so the expected CRITICAL 'has NO master' line was absent and the assertion failed. A real defect showed up in the same run: the returning ex-master was probed as an idle follower, counted as unfit, and its correct re-seating was logged 'PROMOTION NOT LOSS-FREE ... LAST RESORT', a false alarm. Fixes: refillHoldEffects no longer reports an ex-master re-seated on its own partition (2 more flare_unit cases), and the test cordons the single kind node before the kill, so the replacement stays Pending and the hold is exercised; it then uncordons and requires the ex-master to be master again. Re-run pending.

2026-10-03 (PR run 37030725289 on 79bf29c), classified as FUNCTIONAL (operator): with the node cordoned the hold ran as designed (follower Slave/Active balance 0, 'has NO master' logged every pass, no promotion). On the uncordon the follower was promoted anyway, with no NOT LOSS-FREE line. Path: the failed-over ex-master's entry was Proxy/Down with partition -1, so its re-registration fell through to fresh registration ('Proxy, all partitions full'), which drops lastMasterOf; in the next pass assignProxiesPure → autoAssign's zombie-master guard saw a masterless partition with a live Active slave and promoted it, making the ex-master a Prepare slave that would have rebuilt from the far-behind follower, wiping the very writes the hold protects. Fixes: (1) NodeAdd rejoins a Down ex-master (partition -1, lastMasterOf within the CRD's partitions) as a syncing slave of its old partition, keeping lastMasterOf, so the refill's tier 3 re-seats it; (2) autoAssign/findActiveSlaveForPartition take the unfit list (the FSM passes followUnfitKeys): an unfit Active slave is not promoted, and if it is the only candidate the proxy is left unassigned for the refill to decide; (3) a slave's Prepare→Active drops lastMasterOf, so a rejoined ex-master that rebuilt from a newer master stops claiming the newest copy. autoAssign_cle and assignProxiesPure_cle are now stated for every zones/exclusion argument; 6 more flare_unit cases (229 total). The replication-leg failure is CI infrastructure (no test ran): the setup downloads now retry. Re-run pending.

2026-10-03 (PR run 37035470146 on 267a196, all 8 legs green): lag-hold E2E PASS. The follower was 140 positions behind (applied 4 of source 144) and judged unfit; with the ex-master away (node cordoned) it was never promoted and 'partition 0 has NO master' was logged on each pass; after the uncordon the ex-master was master again with all 140 acknowledged items, no NOT LOSS-FREE line was logged for the follower, and the follower rebuilt (reconstruction_started 2) and followed it with 140 items. One run on kind; the wait-expiry and empty-ex-master branches are covered by flare_unit only.

2026-10-03 (PR run 37103800886, all 8 legs green): both release paths of the lag hold PASS end to end. tmpfs: the master pod returned empty, the follower (unfit, applied 4 of source 144) was seated at once and logged NOT LOSS-FREE, and the empty ex-master rebuilt from it and followed (77 items each; the follower kept catching up slowly until the kill, so 140 − 77 acknowledged writes are the accepted asynchronous loss). Wait expiry (60 s, ex-master kept away by a cordon): the hold was logged first and the follower was seated after 117 s, not before 60 s, with NOT LOSS-FREE; the returning ex-master followed it (77 items). The 117 s is the wait plus dead detection plus the masterless clock starting on the pass after the failover: in production, expect the configured wait plus about one minute.

2026-10-03 (PR run 37107011336): per-partition lag hold on 2p x 2r PASS — only P1's follower was cut and behind (applied 6 of source 120) and judged unfit; with P1's master killed and kept away, P1 was held (its follower not promoted, 'partition 1 has NO master' logged) while P0 kept its master and took writes (40 attempted through it: its own 32 keys STORED, P0 items 126→158; the 8 P1 keys failed, as the hold implies); the breaker did not trip (1 of 4 unavailable); P1's ex-master returned as master with all 114 items and no NOT LOSS-FREE line was logged for P1's follower.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37296281060 on ac49d67; NOT independently reviewed). PRODUCT DEFECT, failover lag bound (CHECK-06-laghold test 25; it had passed in 37283759673 and 37290297021, so it is timing-dependent). While the ex-master was away the hold worked ('NOT promoted while the ex-master is away', logged at ticks 26-28). When the ex-master's pod returned, NodeAdd rejoined it correctly as a Prepare slave of P0 with lastMasterOf kept. In the SAME pass (tick 29) the refill crowned the follower that was 140 positions behind: 'PROMOTION NOT LOSS-FREE … the wait for the ex-master ended or the ex-master came back empty'. The ex-master then rebuilt from it ('ex-master master again=false'). Cause (code): Bridge.dataBearingPodKeys leaves out a pod whose stats probe FAILS ('Best-effort: a pod whose probe fails is simply not listed'), and K8sReconciler.exMasterBackEmpty treats 'live and not listed' as 'came back empty'. A returning ex-master that cannot be read yet (the pass before, the operator logged 'Invalid IP address' for it) therefore ends the hold. Unknown is taken as known-empty; the same pattern affects the refill tier's empty-master guard. Proposed fix (not implemented): the probe returns known-empty and unknown separately; the hold ends only on a KNOWN empty ex-master or on the wait budget; a unit check for 'ex-master live but unreadable keeps the hold', and a seam test delaying the returning ex-master's stats.

2026-10-06 (implemented in 616a010, CI pending; NOT reviewed). Fix for the CI 37296281060 lag-hold defect. The data probe now classifies data-bearing / KNOWN-empty / Unknown. Known-empty requires a complete reply with a well-formed curr_items 0, and the pod's UID and restart count unchanged across the probe; a missing restart count is not a match. No IP, exec/stats failure, or a truncated or malformed reply is Unknown. Observations are per pass and never reused. The hold and the refill tiers no longer treat absence from the data-bearing list as emptiness: exMasterBackEmpty uses only the known-empty list. Unknown never releases the hold. Release by the wait budget is logged as the accepted-loss policy ('EXPIRED'), separately from 'READ empty' and 'hold disabled'. Remaining: the refill's empty-master guard still falls back to crowning the lastMasterOf holder when NO copy in the partition is known to hold data (the original 'no information' behaviour); this favours the newest copy and is not changed here.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37386580971 on e1b90cb; NOT independently reviewed). This is the first CI run with the lag-hold fix. continuous-replication-lag-hold-unreadable PASSED: the returning ex-master was live and unreadable for 90 s, over 19 blocked probe passes, and the far-behind follower was never crowned (no NOT LOSS-FREE line). After unblocking, the ex-master was master again with 140/140 acknowledged items. The tmpfs suite (ex-master truly empty) and the expiry suite also passed with their new reason assertions ('READ empty' / 'EXPIRED'), and the base lag-hold test passed. One passing run; the original failure was timing-dependent.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37392833616 on 459c800; NOT independently reviewed). Multipart lag hold (CHECK-06-holdmp) FAILED on its hold-line assertion. The product outcome was correct: P1's far-behind follower was NOT promoted, P0 kept its master and took 40 writes, and the breaker did not trip. But the follower held NO P1 data when its master was killed ('P1 items master=114 replica=0'). The hold line lists only DATA-BEARING held followers, and an empty follower is never crowned by the data-bearing tiers, so there was nothing to list. The heldForExMaster logic is unchanged by the lag-hold fix. The earlier passes depended on the follower applying some data before the cut took effect. Test change: write 40 keys first and require P1's follower to hold the master's P1 count before the cut. Open observability question: a partition left masterless with only an EMPTY follower logs no CRITICAL hold line.
controls.call_path: NodeAdd rejoin -> Slave/Prepare; FSM failover/RecoveryRefill -> promoteMasterlessPartitions -> promoteMasterlessPartition.

checks.procedure: Cover total restart, known empty vs unknown, surviving Active and Prepare copies; document expected loss/availability policy. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

Failover lag bound end to end and in the pure refill. flare_unit checkFailoverLagHold: hold off crowns the unfit follower (previous behaviour); hold on with the ex-master away leaves the partition masterless and reports it; an ex-master back with data is crowned; back empty, or the partition in the expired list, crowns the follower; a fit follower is crowned at once. E2E continuous-replication-lag-hold (PVC, 1p x 2r, bound 20 positions, wait 900 s): the follower is throttled to one WAL batch per second (repl-follow-max-batches 1, repl-follow-batch-delay-usec 1000000) with the master's forwards cut, so it stays connected and knows its backlog; once the operator judges it unfit the master pod is force-deleted; the follower must never become master, the CRITICAL 'has NO master' line must appear, the ex-master must be master again with every acknowledged write, and the follower must follow it again.

E2E continuous-replication-lag-hold-tmpfs (replication leg): tmpfs, 1p x 2r, bound 20, wait 900 s; the throttled follower is judged unfit, then the master pod is deleted and returns EMPTY. The follower must be seated (nothing to wait for), the NOT LOSS-FREE line must be logged for it, and the empty ex-master must rebuild from it and follow with equal items.

E2E continuous-replication-lag-hold-expiry (breaker-migration leg): PVC, bound 20, wait 60 s; the node is cordoned so the ex-master stays away. The hold must be logged first, the follower must be seated only after at least 60 s, with the NOT LOSS-FREE line; after the uncordon the ex-master (with the writes the follower never got) must follow the new master with equal items — the accepted loss.

E2E continuous-replication-multipart-lag-hold (wal-recovery leg): 2p x 2r PVC, bound 20, wait 900 s, throttled followers; only P1's forwards are cut, so only P1's follower falls behind and is judged unfit; the node is cordoned and P1's master is force-deleted. P1 must be held (its follower not promoted, 'partition 1 has NO master' logged); P0 must keep its master and take writes meanwhile; the breaker must not trip (1 of 4 unavailable); after the uncordon P1's ex-master must be master again with every acknowledged item, with no NOT LOSS-FREE line for P1's follower.

Failover lag bound with an UNREADABLE returning ex-master (CI 37296281060 defect). Unit: flare_unit checkFailoverLagHold (unreadable ex-master keeps the hold; a known-empty reading of a non-live pod does not end it; NOT LOSS-FREE reason EXPIRED vs READ empty). E2E continuous-replication-lag-hold-unreadable (repair leg): the follower is cut and judged unfit, the master pod is killed with the node cordoned, the operator's data probe is told (seam FLARE_TEST_STATS_BLOCK) that the returning ex-master cannot be read; for 90 s with the ex-master live and unreadable (>= 3 blocked probe passes) the follower must never be crowned and no NOT LOSS-FREE line may appear; once readable the ex-master is master again with every acknowledged write. The tmpfs suite (ex-master truly empty) must log the reason 'READ empty' and the expiry suite 'EXPIRED'.

FINDING 2026-10-02 (CI 36914077401, functional, fixed; PR run 36918285987 green incl. prepare-evidence): the NotReady streak that turns a present-but-NotReady pod into a dead node was counted regardless of the node's state. A node is NotReady for its whole Prepare/reconstruction (sync-gated readiness), so it carried a long streak and was declared dead in the very pass it became Active, before its pod could observe the activation. Seen in prepare-evidence: PREPARE-REPAIR activated the slave, the wall-clock grace ended 124 s in, and the next pass failed the slave over (it was masked before by the longer cycle-based grace and by the breaker tripping at 1 of 2). Fix: K8sReconciler.unreadyStreaks counts only while the node is an Active master/slave in the committed map; a Prepare node's streak restarts at 0. Three unit cases.

2026-10-05 SAF-08 audit (docs/reports/2026-10-05-saf08-copy-identity-audit.md): apart from the empty-master delete (UID precondition), no delete or promote decision bound its evidence to a pod UID or flared process; protection was only the re-registration (regEpoch) merge, which misses a replaced pod that has not registered yet. Fixed: (a) an Active slave whose pod is not Ready is not a promotion candidate in failover, drain, refill or the zombie guard (readiness is sync-gated, so a same-name replacement is never Ready before it registers); (b) replica-repair demotion is deferred unless the partition's CURRENT master is known to hold data, and the demotion is an atomic re-check of the entry (regEpoch); (c) PREPARE-REPAIR re-reads the slave's boot id just before activating and requires an unchanged regEpoch. Open: the self-heal's validated successor is not pinned for the following drain; stuck-Down restart deletes by name on stale state; data-bearing evidence is not UID-bound and all-probes-failed can crown an empty lastMasterOf holder; the first follow reading after an operator restart is never marked as a process change; the zone-repair swap. CI pending.

2026-10-05 review corrections: (a) Readiness is a snapshot, not identity — excluding NotReady candidates closes the window BEFORE a replacement registers, not a restart/replacement AFTER the observation; now every node a pass promotes must still be the incarnation observed in that pass (pod UID and flared container restart count, from the pod list) when the commit happens, else the pass is dropped and not persisted (commitChecked; test seam FLARE_TEST_PROMOTION_BARRIER). (b) The empty-master self-heal's UID precondition protects the delete target only; the surviving successor's incarnation is now bracketed around its fresh stats and must be stable, and the validated successor is pinned for the following drain while its pod stays that incarnation. (c) Repair demotion: the source's stats are bracketed by its incarnation and the atomic update requires the partition's master entry (key and regEpoch) unchanged. (d) An EMPTY repair source is accepted only under the replica's own lineage (rocksdb_master_id: deleted to empty), otherwise deferred — neither 'empty is safe to rebuild from' nor 'empty is never a source'. CI pending.

2026-10-05 review round 2 (implemented, NOT CI-verified): (1) Ready, UID, container restart count and deletionTimestamp now come from ONE pod-list response (parsePodRows); before, two list calls joined by pod name could pair an OLD pod's Ready with a NEW pod's UID. Identity needs both halves observed both times — a missing restart count on both sides is no longer a match. Roles: pod UID + container restart count = Kubernetes' view of the copy's incarnation, used to bind promotion/delete/repair decisions; flared's reconstruction_boot_id = flared's own view of its process, used to bind data-plane statements (follow position, completion records). (2) An EMPTY repair source is accepted only with the replica's lineage AND either the replica's source epoch (deleted to empty in the same history) or an epoch advanced by a BULK rewrite; flared now records why each epoch was minted (rocksdb_source_epoch_reason: new / promotion / bulk / inherited; legacy = unknown). An epoch minted by a promotion (an empty copy promoted) or for an unknown reason defers. Unit-tested (flare_unit, cutter test_source_epoch_reason_recorded_and_persisted); E2E covers delete-to-empty (copy-identity) and the flush_all recovery path (continuous-replication bulk test); promotion of an empty copy is not staged in E2E.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37283759673 on 8ada54f; NOT independently reviewed). copy-identity tests 10-13 PASSED: a same-name replacement and a process restart were never promoted, and the restart and the replacement after observation were each ABORTED at commit with the other slave taking over with every key. These passes ran with the suite's test-only breaker floor (minUnavailableToTrip 3): they are evidence for copy identity ONLY, NOT for recovery under the production breaker setting. Test 14 (legitimately emptied master) FAILED. This is a PRODUCT-RULE limitation, not a harness error. The operator deferred the repair indefinitely, logging 'the current master holds 0 keys and its source epoch (5:34b28a9d-…) is not the replica's (4:31d0ef6c-…) and was advanced by promotion, not a bulk rewrite … the request stays pending' (breaker-migration report). In legacy (non-follow) mode a replica does not adopt the source epoch through dump reconstruction or a promotion, so after ANY earlier promotion in the cluster a deleted-to-empty master cannot be told from an empty promoted copy under the current rule. The behaviour is safe (no rebuild from an unproven empty source) but not live: the replica stays out of sync until a human acts. A design decision is needed (epoch adoption on reconstruction or re-seat vs a human-approved resolution); it is not implemented.

2026-10-05 review round (implemented, CI pending; NOT reviewed). Decision: option A, conditioned. flared records REBUILD EVIDENCE (__flare_repl_rebuilt_from = source master_id, source epoch, and this node's own epoch at recording) only after a clean truncate + full dump whose source advertised the same non-empty master_id and source epoch in a features probe at the dump's start and a fresh probe at its end. It is a separate reserved key, NOT the source-epoch field: the local source epoch gates forwarded changes (_decide_change), so adopting the source's epoch there would also accept the source's change stream — a claim about position this evidence must not make. The evidence is dropped durably before every rebuild attempt (a rebuild does not start if it cannot be dropped), on every advance of the node's own epoch (promotion, truncate/flush_all), by a snapshot swap (which also drops the source's copied evidence) and by a wiped DB; evidence recorded under another own epoch is ignored at load, so a lost delete cannot resurrect it. Merge dumps, WAL catch-up and master reconstructions record none. The operator accepts an empty source when lineage matches and the replica's evidence names exactly the master's master_id and epoch (StatsObservation.repairSourceVerdict (c)); otherwise the existing rule (same epoch, or a bulk epoch) applies. Limits: a replica that caught up by WAL sync after a promotion, or was restored by snapshot from a different epoch, still defers (safe, not live); option B (a one-shot human approval bound to the target copy and the source history) is NOT implemented; test seams FLARE_TEST_DISABLE_SNAPSHOT_BOOTSTRAP / FLARE_TEST_DISABLE_WAL_RECONSTRUCTION are E2E-only environment variables.

checks.procedure: Exercise missing pods, sustained NotReady, failed API listing, lone unhealthy master and multiple pods on a lost worker. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

SAF-08 copy identity (audit docs/reports/2026-10-05-saf08-copy-identity-audit.md). E2E copy-identity (1p x 3r PVC, legacy replication, drain 20 s): (1) a slave is force-deleted with the node cordoned so its same-name replacement stays Pending while the map says Active, then the master is drained — the replaced pod must never be master, the healthy slave must take over with every key, and the operator must log the replaced pod as withheld; (2) a slave's flared is killed -9 (same pod, new process) and the master is drained at once — that slave must not be promoted, the other takes over with every key (the restart-to-registration window is short: an outcome guard). Post-observation (promotion barrier FLARE_TEST_PROMOTION_BARRIER): (3) the pass that chose a successor is held after its observations, that successor's flared is killed, and on release the operator must log PROMOTION ABORTED for it and a later pass promote a valid copy with every key; (4) the same with the chosen successor replaced under the same name (node cordoned): aborted, the other slave takes over. (The former test 5, a legitimately emptied master, FAILED in 37283759673 and 37290297021: a product limitation of those revisions (the repair was deferred forever). It is addressed by the rebuild evidence (daceb41) and its verification moved to CHECK-07-emptysource. Under the new rule a replica that caught up by WAL sync after a promotion still defers: that residual limitation is recorded, not resolved.)

SAF-08 empty repair source proven by rebuild evidence (review 2026-10-05). Unit: flare_unit checkRepairSource (empty promoted master accepted only when the replica's rebuild evidence names exactly its master_id AND epoch; an earlier epoch, another lineage, missing or partial evidence defer); cutter test_rebuild_evidence_rule, test_rebuild_evidence_persisted_and_cleared, test_rebuild_evidence_persist_failure, test_swap_in_snapshot_drops_source_rebuild_evidence. E2E empty-source (wal-recovery leg; 1p x 3r PVC, legacy replication, test seams FLARE_TEST_DISABLE_SNAPSHOT_BOOTSTRAP and FLARE_TEST_DISABLE_WAL_RECONSTRUCTION force every rebuild through truncate + full dump, --reconstruction-bwlimit 128 makes a 6.4 MB dump last ~50 s): (1) after a promotion the ex-master rejoins, is rebuilt by full dump and records the current master's master_id and epoch although its own epoch differs; (2) every key deleted on that master while the rebuilt replica misses the deletes: the repair is accepted and the replica rebuilt to empty, not deferred; (3) a replica carrying evidence is restarted and killed again mid-dump: no evidence from the first dump's start until a dump completes, the interrupted process records none, final evidence names the master; (4) the master is drained while a replica dumps from it: the interrupted dump records nothing, the evidence finally names the NEW master's epoch, never the old one; (5) a copy is promoted (new epoch, same master_id) and its keys deleted while a replica whose evidence names the earlier epoch misses them: the repair DEFERS and the replica keeps every key.

Copy retention phases 3, 4 and 7 (docs/design-copy-retention.md §3-§5, §8-§10), verified as ONE unit (user instruction 2026-10-07). A replica's copy is replaced only by a staged copy: full dump or snapshot into data_dir/staging-<attempt>, epoch-bound WAL replay of (L0, L1] to a fixed target L1, a final check, the protection rule right before the switch, a durable seal, the switch (the old copy retained), a post-switch catch-up; no truncate and no discard-first remain on that path. Legacy (epoch-less) sources: the position must equal L0 at L1, right before the switch and after it (interval evidence only; the write stop is held OUTSIDE until the replica is Active). Capacity: source copy size + rebuildReserveBytes must fit (unset = stop, rebuild_blocked=reserve_unset); the copy stops before eating the reserve (no_space). Concurrency: one snapshot serve per source (busy), one NEW rebuild assignment per partition and per cluster (REBUILD HELD). Unit (cutter): test_staged_dump_then_replay_matches_the_source_and_switches, test_staging_abandoned_and_left_over, test_snapshot_serve_one_at_a_time_in_its_own_dir, test_copy_switch retained/capacity cases; flare_unit checkRebuildConcurrency. E2E: copy-protection (H1 and Unknown at the switch gate), empty-source test 1 (staged full dump, evidence), continuous-replication-rebuild-tmpfs (no room: stop and notify, nothing discarded), continuous-replication-upgrade (rc56 -> this build by the release procedure, legacy staged rule). NOT yet covered: two replicas requesting a snapshot at once (§11.4), the space watch stopping a copy mid-way in E2E, quarantine (phase 5), approvals (phase 6), the stats-based running count.

Copy retention phases 5 and 6 (design §6, §7). Quarantine: the marker is durable BEFORE the corrupt copy moves (quarantine-<copy-id>) and BEFORE the empty copy exists; the post-quarantine copy reports rocksdb_quarantined=1, binds no read source, and is a deferred repair source for the operator; one generation (rebuild_blocked=quarantine_full: nothing moved or deleted); a verified staged switch replaces it, and the marker is removed with the retained copy under the §8 conditions. Approvals: FlareCopyDiscardApproval (clusterUID, podUID, copyId, requestId, operation discard-retained | discard-quarantine | discard-before-copy, expiresAt). The operator relays only its own cluster's approvals, refuses unknown operations, malformed tokens and a replaced pod, and marks expired ones without sending them. flared records the requestId durably before deleting anything and answers a repeat from that record (a refusal is consumed too). A live copy is discarded only on a node that is neither master nor Active slave, and only with consistent identity records. Unit (cutter): test_quarantine_marker_crash_points_and_one_generation, test_copy_discard_approval_is_named_and_one_shot, test_copy_discard_frees_the_quarantine_generation; flare_unit checkCopyDiscardApproval. E2E: copy-retention test 3 (applied once, repeat answered from the record, stale copy refused, other pod refused, expired not sent). NOT covered by E2E: a real corruption leading to quarantine.

constraint.text: Circuit-breaker policy pauses mass failover; configured recovery refill is a separate path.

controls.title: Limit mass-failure changes
scenarios: Many Active nodes become dead candidates; hysteresis holds; auto-reset disabled.
assumptions: Breaker thresholds use observed Active/dead population, not actual data health.
residual_risks: Correlated worker faults are not modeled explicitly; autoResetEnabled=false parks refill.

FINDING (2026-09-14, pre-existing, not changed by this branch): detectDeadNodesPure excludes nodes already Down and nodes in Prepare, so circuitBreakerDecision's deadCount is the number of nodes that became dead in THIS tick against the whole map; the 50% trip needs half the cluster to vanish inside one 5s tick. Deaths that straddle ticks (25% + 25% on a 4-node cluster) never trip and failover proceeds one node at a time. A pod-less node left in Prepare is never counted dead. Seen once in CI (third run at 5e80d73, no trip in 480s, steady M=2 S=0 D=2 P=1 with the map version advancing +7 per tick); the same leg tripped at 10-15s in three other runs and locally. Whether the breaker should count the cluster's dead fraction (Down included) is a design change outside SAF-01..07; not fixed here. FIX (2026-10-01, CI pending): the breaker now counts nodes unavailable now (breakerUnavailableKeys: dead this tick + already Down + pod-less Prepare); thresholds and hysteresis unchanged; breakerUnavailable_ge_dead proves the count never shrinks below this tick's deaths. Definition chosen by the author after the user asked to fix existing problems; reviewer to confirm. See docs/reports/2026-10-01-saf11-breaker-unavailable.md.

SAF-11 definition consequences (2026-10-01): a long-standing Down node keeps counting toward the trip threshold, lowering the margin for later failures; while tripped, a tick with no new deaths now runs the reset hysteresis instead of silently resetting.

FINDING 2026-10-02 (design review, not a regression): with the default threshold (50%), a cluster of one partition x two replicas trips the breaker on the death of a single node, before and after the SAF-11 count change (1 of 2 = 50%). Failover is then paused: a dead master is not replaced by its slave and the partition takes no writes until the master pod returns (from its PVC; on tmpfs it returns empty). Every failover E2E runs 2 partitions x 2 replicas (one death = 25%), so this was never exercised. Deployments of 1 master + 1 slave need either a different threshold, a minimum cluster size below which the breaker does not trip on a single death, or acceptance that failover is manual. Decision for the user.

DECISION 2026-10-02 (user: recommended option): the breaker never trips with fewer than minUnavailableToTrip unavailable nodes (CR circuitBreaker.minUnavailableToTrip, default 2), so a single failed node in a 1-partition x 2-replica cluster no longer pauses failover. Proofs circuitBreakerDecision_trips (now with the floor as a hypothesis) and circuitBreakerDecision_below_min_no_trip; unit cases 1-of-2 no trip, floor 1 restores it, 2-of-4 still trips. The SAF-11 count definition is confirmed by the user. CI pending.
controls.call_path: AfterDetectDead computes breaker state -> EmergencyPaused or RecoveryRefill; trippedRef carries hysteresis.

checks.procedure: Run breaker scenarios including auto-reset disabled and recovery refill; confirm no unintended mass demotion. Referenced suites are starting points to extend, not evidence that this scenario is already covered.

2026-10-06 PRE-EXISTING PRODUCT DEFECT found by empty-source test 4 (PR run 37386580971; NOT independently reviewed). A reconstruction handler keeps the source it was created with for its whole retry loop (handler_reconstruction::run: up to 60 attempts, 2-30 s apart, about 30 min) and never re-reads the partition's current master. After the source master is drained and another node promoted, the rebuilding replica keeps retrying the ex-master (observed: 35 attempts against the drained master). It cannot finish meanwhile, and if the ex-master came back as a non-master it could dump from it. Proposal for review (not implemented): each attempt re-resolves the partition's master from the current map and abandons a source that is no longer the partition's master.

2026-10-06 (implemented in 380726e, CI pending; NOT reviewed). Fix for the reconstruction-source defect. Every attempt of a slave's reconstruction re-reads its partition's master from the current map; none = wait with nothing copied; this node = abandon. Once the handler has truncated the copy or started a dump, a source change forces a CLEAN next attempt (truncate, no WAL catch-up), so histories are never merged. A merely attempted WAL catch-up does not count, so the 'source not newer' guard still protects an untouched full copy. Before completion (evidence, activation) the source must still be the partition's master; otherwise the copy is not activated. E2E: empty-source test 4 (old master drained while REACHABLE) and a new test (old master UNREACHABLE). Remaining risk: after a completion refused by the re-check, the forced clean rebuild copies the CURRENT master even when it holds less (e.g. an empty promoted copy); that case is left to the operator's empty-master guards.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37407630865 on bf096f0; NOT independently reviewed). Reconstruction re-selection, first run. empty-source test 4 PASSED: the old master was drained while still REACHABLE, its completed dump was handled, and the final evidence names the promoted master's epoch. The new test 5 (old master UNREACHABLE: node cordoned, pod force-deleted) FAILED, and the replica's log shows why: 'connect() failed: Connection timed out (110)'. connection_tcp::_open used a BLOCKING connect with no deadline (8 retries), so an attempt against a vanished pod that never answers with a RST waits the kernel's SYN timeout on every retry (~15 min per attempt). The re-selection at the next attempt never came within the test. Fix (implemented, CI pending): an opt-in connect deadline (3 s, one retry) on every reconstruction and follower connection; other connection users unchanged. Test 6 failed its precondition as a consequence.

2026-10-06 review (implemented, CI pending; NOT reviewed). ACTIVATION BOUNDARY: the completion re-check was not enough, because _activate_with_retry then made up to 30 activation attempts without looking at the source again. Every attempt now first re-validates the source: the partition's master in the current map is the same node, and a fresh probe shows the same master_id and source epoch. A same-name source with a NEW epoch (re-promoted, restored, flush_all) is treated as a change, separately from a change of node. Unknown (probe failed) is not valid. On failure the copy is not activated and the next reconstruction attempt starts clean from the current master. E2E: activation held by a test seam while (a) the master is drained, or (b) the same master is flush_all'ed. FORCE-CLEAN, stated precisely: the 'source not newer' guard is BYPASSED only when THIS handler already truncated the copy or started a dump into it (so the local copy is no longer an intact older history), or when a completed copy was refused at completion/activation. In those cases the replica is rebuilt from the CURRENT master even if that master holds fewer keys, or an older or emptier history. The loss accepted is this replica's partial copy, or its completed copy of the previous source's history. It is NOT a comparison of item counts and NOT a judgement of which history is better: the current master is taken as authoritative. 'Never mix two histories' holds. 'Never lose a better copy' does NOT hold in these cases: a better copy on this replica, already partly overwritten, is not protected here. The operator's empty-master guards cover only EMPTY masters, not stale non-empty ones.

2026-10-06 (PR run 37414948177 on 665bfb8; NOT independently reviewed). ACTIVATION BOUNDARY, first CI run. Test 7 PASSED: while a replica's activation was held, flush_all on the SAME master (still master, same name) advanced its source epoch, and the activation was STOPPED as a history change. Test 6, the master change: the held activation was STOPPED ('activation STOPPED before attempt 6: the partition's master is now empty-source-nodes-1 … not the source empty-source-nodes-0'), but the test then failed its rebuilt-with-new-epoch check. Tests 4 and 5 failed the same check, the evidence/epoch comparison. HARNESS, with the log as basis: the test read the promoted master's epoch IMMEDIATELY after the operator's map showed it as master, i.e. before flared's own promotion advance. In test 4 the evidence named 3:6e079da6-…; the same node (empty-source-nodes-1) shows exactly that epoch as master at the start of test 5 (its read value 2:f73f… was pre-promotion). In test 5, empty-source-nodes-0 went 9:… (read) -> 10:… (named by the evidence). The tests now wait for the promoted node's epoch to move from its pre-fault value before comparing. Test 5's source re-selection itself worked this time ('source re-selected to empty-source-nodes-0=true') with the connect deadline. Test 8 failed its precondition as a consequence. NOT independently reviewed; the race classification rests on the log values quoted.

constraint.text: A future replication design must specify what acknowledged writes survive and how replicas catch up after interruption.

controls.title: Bound replication durability guarantees
scenarios: Replica unavailable through WAL retention; asynchronous drop after client success; master failover.

SAF-10 answers this control's subject on the RocksDB backend: the design states what a replica may claim (a contiguous applied position, never a connection or a past reconstruction) and how it catches up after an interruption (resume from the cursor; explicit needs_rebuild when the history is gone). Implementation and evidence live under EV-16..EV-20; acknowledged-write semantics are UNCHANGED — forwarding is still asynchronous and a write acknowledged to the client can still be lost if the master dies before the follower applies it.
assumptions: Current live replication is op-level forwarding; WAL is used for reconstruction/bootstrap only.
residual_risks: No continuous WAL replication; adding master LSNs alone does not establish durable acknowledgement semantics.

Replication is still asynchronous end to end: the master answers the client before the follower has applied, so continuous WAL replication removes the SILENT-gap failure, not the loss window on master death (design §5.3; the FSM logs an unproven promotion as NOT LOSS-FREE).

RESOURCE FLOOR, found by the scale evaluation (report 2026-09-21-saf10d-t6-t9-scale.txt): flared's RocksDB defaults budget ≈704 MB (512 MB block cache + 3 × 64 MB write buffers) before flared's own memory, so a 512Mi container is OOMKilled under write load (observed, exit 137 at 2m42s of a 2M-key load). The shipped chart's node default is limits.memory 1Gi and the FlareCluster CRD exposes no blockCacheSizeMb / writeBufferSizeMb / maxWriteBufferNumber, so the floor cannot be lowered through the chart. Not fixed in this PR.

WAL retention cap overshoot (from the SAF-10 long-outage evaluation, report 2026-09-30-sustained-after-more-fix.md): with a trailing follower the archive grew to 499 MB past a 256 MB cap before any purge; on tmpfs this is RAM. The chart's tmpfs guidance ('cap it well under tmpfs.sizeLimit') must account for the overshoot, not just the cap.

DECISION 2026-10-02 (user): asynchronous durability is accepted for production; RPO = replication lag at master data loss. The lagged-successor E2E records the gap. Client-visible behaviour: flared option read-unavailable-error (CR spec.rocksdb.readUnavailableError, default false) answers SERVER_ERROR instead of a miss when a get cannot be served; enable it where flare is the primary store. op_get change compiled only by the CI image and nix builds; no E2E exercises the option yet.

2026-10-02: E2E for read-unavailable-error added (continuous-replication suite): with replica->master traffic to 12121 rejected and the follower disconnected, a get on the replica must answer SERVER_ERROR with the option on and END (miss) with it off; each switch confirmed by flared's reload notice. CI pending.

2026-10-02 (CI 36938834526), INCONCLUSIVE: the first read-unavailable-error E2E got an EMPTY reply from the replica within nc's 5 s idle timeout (option confirmed on by the reload notice, follower disconnected). Most likely the forward to the master was still retrying with reconnects; the test now waits up to 40 s, times the reply and prints the replica's flared lines on failure. Not recorded as a pass.

2026-10-02 (CI 36941388055): read-unavailable-error E2E PASS. With replica->master traffic rejected and the follower disconnected, a get on the replica answered 'SERVER_ERROR read unavailable' with the option on and 'END' (miss) with it off. Both replies took 18 s: the forward to the master retries with reconnects before it is given up, so a client whose read timeout is shorter than that sees a timeout instead of either reply. The retry/timeout budget of forwarded reads is not tuned for this case.

2026-10-06 pf-dev observation (operational; NOT a CI result). After the slave nodes-1 was deleted (UID-preconditioned, normal grace) and rebuilt on rc65, the rebuild path was: snapshot from the rc56 master refused BEFORE the swap ('the staged checkpoint carries no source epoch'), then truncate + full dump. Items matched (15,854,750 on both) and there were no restarts. But the slave's tmpfs was at 7.6 GB of 8 GB, of which 4.6 GB was the RocksDB WAL ARCHIVE written by the dump, retained by rocksdb-wal-ttl-seconds 86400 / wal-size-limit-mb 10240, both larger than the pod. Its memory cgroup read 8.42 GB of 8.59 GB. On tmpfs the WAL retention budget counts against the memory limit (UCA-27 on a replica): a full-dump rebuild on tmpfs can leave the replica one burst away from an OOM kill. No action taken (instruction: stop and report). Options for review: size the WAL retention to the tmpfs/memory budget in the CR, or skip archiving the replica's own dump WAL. CORRECTION (2026-10-06 03:00 UTC, read-only re-check): pf-dev's actual settings are rocksdb-wal-ttl-seconds 10800 (3 h) and rocksdb-wal-size-limit-mb 1024, not the defaults (86400 / 10240) quoted above. RocksDB deletes archived WAL itself at its periodic purge: past the size limit, and past the TTL. Between purges the archive can exceed the limit, and the full dump wrote ~4.6 GB faster than a purge ran; that is when nodes-1 peaked at its memory limit (memory.max_usage_in_bytes 8,584,912,896 of 8,589,934,592; failcnt 0). By 03:00 the archive was 67 MB and nodes-1 used 3.69 GB. The master nodes-0 is now the tighter one: 7.33 GB of 8 GB (5.58 GB tmpfs + 1.69 GB RSS), with 2.69 GB of blob files against the replica's 0.45 GB for the same 15,854,750 items (enable_blob_garbage_collection=false, so overwritten blob values are never reclaimed). 20-minute trend sampled every 2 min. CORRECTION 2 (review 2026-10-06): 'changing WAL retention needs a restart, and on tmpfs a restart means a full rebuild' conflated three events. (1) A flared PROCESS/CONTAINER restart in the same pod keeps an emptyDir (medium: Memory) volume; pf-dev's container command only creates /data/flare and removes the pid file, so the DB is reopened from tmpfs and the option takes effect without a rebuild. This does NOT make a restart safe now: a master restart still takes it out of service. (2) A POD replacement (delete, StatefulSet update) loses the tmpfs. (3) The APPLICATION itself can discard the DB: hard_reset, emergency empty reopen, restore-sentinel discard. Other caveats: the 2.69 GB of master blob files is not all garbage (live values above min_blob_size live there too); equal item counts on both nodes are not equal content; and the rebuild's peak at the memory limit remains the deciding fact. Master update stays ON HOLD. Next product items: blob GC configuration and observability; WAL/tmpfs capacity control INCLUDING DURING a rebuild. Releasing WAL early after a rebuild does not prevent the mid-rebuild peak. No manual WAL deletion, and no WAL disabling without verified durability.

constraint.text: Continuous fetch resumes without external intervention, and a lost connection alone never triggers a rebuild.

controls.title: Resume continuous fetch; a lost connection never rebuilds
scenarios: Link cut and healed with no new writes: the follower reconnects with backoff and resumes from its applied position; the operator's ledger holds the counted drop under the follower's ownership and closes it by position; the follower's stats are unreadable to the operator while a drop is counted (Unknown holds, no demotion).
Repeated cuts, a mid-batch disconnect and an operator restart while cut are NOT yet staged.
assumptions: flared owns delivery and reconnection; the operator only observes. Ownership is the mode (repl-follow-enabled), not the connection state.
residual_risks: Failover: survivors rebuild rather than resume from a per-source cursor (design §9 decision 6).
Only one cut/heal cycle is staged; T5 (repeated cuts) and T8 (operator restart) remain.
The follower's backoff and poll interval are fixed configuration; no load measurement (T17 deferred).

Until 325a2f8 the follower handler RETURNED on needs_rebuild, giving its thread back to the pool while cluster still referenced it; the later stop_wal_follower shut down a pooled thread, which exited without leaving the pool, and the reconstruction handler that was to rebuild the node was triggered on that dead thread and never ran (found by the SAF-10d bulk-operation scenario, runs 3-4). Fixed: terminal outcomes park the thread until the controller's shutdown. E2E confirmation pending (run 5).

THROUGHPUT CEILING (scale run 5, 2M keys): the follower requests at most repl-follow-max-batches (256) batches per poll every repl-follow-poll-interval-usec (200 ms), so the stream cannot exceed ≈1,280 changes/s at the default settings — measured 650-1,270 changes/s while draining. Forwarding carried the data throughout (wal_applied=0, wal_skipped=2,008,010), but a trailing applied position withholds replica reads (lag bound), keeps a repair entry open and lengthens the post-cut catch-up. Whether the stream keeps up at a steady write rate is the separate continuous-replication-sustained evaluation; the defaults are not tuned in this PR.

Boot cost of the exact key scan at open: 0.48-0.98 us/key measured at 0.8M / 1.5M / 2.0M keys (854 / 1503 / 960 ms); a 15.8M-key DB extrapolates to ≈8-16 s of extra start-up. Extrapolation, not a measurement.

SUSTAINED-RATE RESULT (evaluation run 1): the stream stays exactly caught up (lag 0 every window) at 300 and 900 keys/s and FALLS BEHIND monotonically at 2000 keys/s (lag 35,265 → 294,615 over four minutes), draining in 442 s once the load stops. Content never diverges — forwarding carries every write — so this is a POSITION deficit: withheld replica reads, repair entries open longer, longer post-cut catch-up. The run does NOT establish disk behaviour: no memtable flush occurred (768k small records under a 64 MB write buffer), so the flat WAL and data-dir figures are an artefact of the window, and WAL retention for a TRAILING follower was never exercised.

SUSTAINED-RATE RESULT after the MORE scheduling fix (7e979b0, CI run 36707861123, report 2026-09-30-sustained-after-more-fix.md): lag 0 at 300 and 900 keys/s; at 2000 keys/s the stream held for ~90 s then fell behind at ≈+18k/min (≈1,700 changes/s sustained; lag 67,016 after four minutes, drained in 35-43 s). Run 1's 294,615 / 442 s are history of the old code. Disk behaviour is still not established (no flush in the window).

LONG-OUTAGE RESULT, run 1 (c33fe5d, CI 36725778961): phase A (150 MB while cut, three flushes) caught up from the cursor in 11 s with no reconstruction. Phase B: the archived WAL reached 499 MB against a 256 MB WAL_size_limit_MB and was still fully served when healed a few minutes later — RocksDB purges the archive on a periodic check, so the cap is an eventual bound with an overshoot of at least write-rate × purge-interval (≥243 MB here). Capacity must be budgeted as cap + overshoot; the purge interval itself is measured in the next run.

LONG-OUTAGE run 2 (0e49cc7, CI 36731930552): on an IDLE master the archived WAL stayed at 499 MB (cap 256 MB) for 22 minutes with no purge; the purge is driven by flush/compaction cleanup, not by time. Capacity: a master that goes quiet after a burst keeps the overshoot until it writes again.

LONG-OUTAGE run 3 (6e757cb, CI 36741586970): with writes continuing past the cap, one flush cut the archive 499 → 250 MB within 172 s; the follower whose cursor lay in the purged range was told lsn_purged and rebuilt by snapshot in 59 s (items equal, pod unchanged). Archive budget = cap + bytes written between flush/compaction cleanups; an idle master keeps the overshoot (run 2).

2026-10-02 measurements on kind (bound nothing for production hardware). FINDING 2026-10-02 (production enablement gap, fixed CI pending): the continuous-replication flags (repl-identity-forward, repl-follow-enabled, repl-follow-poll-interval-usec) had no CR field. The operator owns extra.conf and rewrites the whole file from spec.rocksdb, so the flags existed only in the E2E seed config; in production there was no supported way to enable follow mode, and any spec.rocksdb change would drop hand-added flags from the file (SIGHUP keeps the in-memory value, the next restart loses it). Now spec.rocksdb.replIdentityForward / replFollowEnabled / replFollowPollIntervalUsec are rendered by the operator (unit case; CRD schema).

2026-10-02 T17 lock hold (run 36941386693, kind): over the whole sustained evaluation the follower applied 772,867 WAL batches under the exclusive _repl_apply_lock for 64.8 s in total (~84 us each); the longest single hold was 294.5 ms, the longest wait to take it exclusively 79 ms, and the longest wait of a forwarded write on it 81 ms. Forwarded writes are therefore delayed by at most ~0.3 s by the follower, not starved. Lag again 0 at 300/900 writes/s and growing at 2000/s.

FINDING 2026-10-02 (run 36941383859, cancelled by the user: 'it takes too long'): with the faster loader the master took ~4.44M keys in ~12 min (~6000 keys/s), then every chunk stored 0 within milliseconds (connections refused: the master most likely restarted, probably OOM at its 2Gi limit), and a `kubectl exec` without a timeout hung the evaluation for 75 min. Suspected, not confirmed: the master forwards every write to a follower that keeps up only to ~2000 writes/s, and the forward queue (max-total-thread-queue default 0 = unlimited) grows in memory. The earlier 15.8M run stopped at ~4.6M too. The evaluation now has a per-chunk timeout, stops after 3 empty chunks and logs the master's restart count, termination reason, RSS and thread queue, and samples them every 500k keys.

FINDING 2026-10-02 (run 36949992433, scale-15m8, FUNCTIONAL — production-relevant): under a ~6000 writes/s load the master's RSS grew linearly with the keys written (44 MB at start, 0.94 GB at 2M, 1.94 GB at 4M; ~470 B per key) while the follower fell far behind (replica forward_applied ~2.57M vs master 4.45M), and the master restarted at ~4.45M keys (restartCount 0 -> 1, almost certainly OOM at the 2Gi limit). Afterwards the master held ~2.62M keys, the follower's count: the far-behind follower was most likely promoted and the old master rebuilt from it, losing ~1.83M acknowledged writes. thread_queue stayed 0, so the growth is not in that counted queue; the suspected holder is the master's buffering of forwards to the slow replica (unconfirmed). This is the asynchronous RPO accepted under A0, but unbounded: memory grows until OOM and the loss is the whole follower backlog. The fail-fast did not trigger because writes kept succeeding on the promoted node, so the evaluation ran 3 h 15 min. Needs: identify the memory holder (heap profile / per-queue stats), bound it so a slow follower costs drops repaired by follow/rebuild instead of an OOM, and cap the backlog at which promotion is allowed.

2026-10-02 diagnosis in progress for the scale memory finding: the forward queue is ruled out (total_thread_queue stayed 0); the sustained run shows RSS growing with keys on BOTH master and replica (~200 B/key at lag 0). The E2E flared pods ran WITHOUT MALLOC_ARENA_MAX (production sets 2 via the chart), so part or all of the growth may be glibc arena fragmentation. E2E pods now set MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, flared exports malloc_in_use_bytes / malloc_free_bytes / malloc_arena_bytes (mallinfo2), the scale evaluation samples them for both nodes, and it stops as soon as the master restarts.

2026-10-02 memory diagnosis, step 1 (run 36975811333, 2M keys at ~3200 keys/s, E2E pods now with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 like production): master RSS 184/229/329 MB at 0.5/1.0/1.5M keys versus 258/373/568 MB without the arena cap (run 36949992433), so glibc arena fragmentation was ~40% of the growth and the earlier OOM at 4.45M keys was largely a test-environment artifact (production pods already set 2). Heap IN USE still grows with keys (117/137/272 MB, ~180 B/key) while free heap stays 40-75 MB: consistent with RocksDB write buffers filling (budget ~384 MB = 64 MB x 3 x 2 CFs, plus 64 MB block cache) but not yet distinguishable from a leak at 2M keys; a 6M-key memory-only run decides. Unrelated to memory: the follower still needed 18.5 min after the load to drain (replica apply ~1.8k forwarded writes/s). Earlier at 0c9be92 every leg of PR run 36973191774 and dispatch 36973187800 failed to BUILD (mallinfo2 without <malloc.h> in the non-RocksDB image, fixed in 431b183); no test ran there.

ROOT CAUSE 2026-10-02 (run 36981303601, 6M keys, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2): the master's heap IN USE grows linearly with no plateau (244 MB at 1M, 800 MB at 3M, 1714 MB at 5.5M keys, ~300 B/key, far past the ~450 MB RocksDB budget) while the replica stays ~100-200 MB, and after the load it falls as the follower catches up (1.75 -> 1.49 GB in 3 min): the master buffers every forward its follower has not taken yet. post_proxy_write enqueues each forward on the replica's proxy thread, and flared's max-total-thread-queue defaults to 0 = unbounded. CORRECTION: the earlier 'forward queue ruled out (total_thread_queue = 0)' was wrong - that stat is sent only by `stats threads queue`, so plain-stats sampling read a missing value as 0. Fix (CI pending): total_thread_queue is now in plain stats; a forward rejected at the bound is counted as proxy_write_dropped for that replica (the repair path sees it, the follower fills it from the WAL) with rate-limited logs; CR spec.rocksdb.maxTotalThreadQueue renders max-total-thread-queue; the chart defaults it to 200000 (~120 MB). Evaluation scale-6m-mem-cap repeats the 6M load with the bound.

2026-10-02 (run 36985410132, 6M keys, max-total-thread-queue = 200000 via the CR): the bound holds. The queue rises to the cap at ~2M keys and stays at ~199k; master heap in use stays 170-235 MB (against 1714 MB unbounded at 5.5M keys) and RSS levels at ~450 MB; no master restart; 3.01M forwards over the cap were counted as proxy_write_dropped. NOT yet shown: that the follower then fills the dropped forwards from the WAL (the memory-only profile does not wait; scale-2m-cap runs the full test with convergence). Also observed: the load took 2495 s against 1179 s unbounded (~2400 vs ~5100 keys/s); the cause of the slowdown is not identified.

2026-10-02 (run 36991784765, 2M keys, cap 100000): the dropped forwards are repaired without a rebuild. 237k forwards were counted dropped by 1.5M keys while master heap in use stayed 104-146 MB; the follower converged to 2,000,000 items equal to the master, taking 527k changes from the WAL (the dropped ones) and 1.47M by forward; reconstruction_completed stayed 1 (the initial copy) and wal_fallback_to_dump 0; kill -9 reopen scanned 2M keys in 1.4 s, data equal. Costs: convergence took 28 min after the load (18.5 min without the cap) and the load ran at ~2060 keys/s (~3200 without the cap): the cause of the slower load is not identified. The bound therefore turns an OOM plus a lossy failover into a slower, complete catch-up; the follower's apply rate (~1.2-1.8k/s on kind) remains the throughput limit.

2026-10-02 throughput variants on b01ff4d (evaluations, not gates). sustained-cpu2 (run 37007519007, flared CPU limit 2): lag 0 in the first and last minute at 300, 900 and 2000 writes/s, KEPT UP at every rate (with the E2E default 500m the run 36941386693 fell behind at 2000/s); replica get p99 per 30 s window 2.9-20.2 ms (max 32.5 ms), reconcile mean 1.6-2.1 s, lease age <= 7 s of 15 s; apply lock hold max 22.8 ms (was 294.5 ms at 500m), forwarded-write wait max 5.6 ms, exclusive-acquire wait max 133 ms. sustained-nrw (run 37007523321, CPU 2 plus noreply-window-limit 16): 300 and 900/s kept up, but 2000/s ended with last-minute lag max 2115 (FELL BEHIND) and reconcile means were higher (1.9-2.6 s); hold max 5.8 ms. Sizing: give flared at least 2 cores where sustained writes reach ~2000/s per partition. One run of each, so the numbers are indicative.

The request now happens in the per-pass ledger step from that pass's classification, against the partition's current master, so the plan acts in the same pass. Probable cause, not verified: the operator re-probes a node whose follow mode it last saw as off only every FLARE_FOLLOW_PROBE_INTERVAL (30) ticks, about 150 s at 5 s ticks, so it learns of the declaration late. A proposed product fix (forget the remembered follow mode when the follow configuration changes) is NOT implemented. The fix is confirmed for correctness of the path, NOT for request latency.

2026-10-05 review round (implemented, CI pending; NOT reviewed). Request latency after enablement: the code re-read a node remembered out of the mode only every FLARE_FOLLOW_PROBE_INTERVAL (30) passes, consistent with the ~2 min gap in PR run 37283759673 but not confirmed as its cause (no per-pass timeline then). Now a change of spec.rocksdb.replFollowEnabled puts every non-Down slave on a CONFIRMATION list: it is read every pass until a complete reading shows the wanted mode, for at most FLARE_FOLLOW_CONFIRM_PASSES (default 120) passes, then back to the interval with a WARNING (bounded, never an unlimited fast poll). An unreadable reading is Unknown and spends a pass; nothing else changes — the repair ledger, boot ids and mode memory follow their own rules. Clearing the memory alone was rejected: a re-read before the file reaches the pod would remember the old mode and wait the full interval again. Limits: only the follow flag triggers it (other config changes do not); the first observation after an operator restart starts no confirmation (every node is unread then and probed anyway).

E2E continuous-replication tests 2-6 (following; cut with create/update/delete; heal with no new writes resumes from the applied position with no rebuild and no pod recreation; ledger held and closed; stats fetch failure held as Unknown).

E2E continuous-replication-limits (T9, bounded): the far-behind replica converges from the position in bounded polls (largest 1 s advance recorded), no reconstruction, master RSS growth within 128 MB. E2E continuous-replication-scale (evaluation, FLARE_E2E_SCALE_KEYS): follower convergence after a pipelined load, exact key scan duration at open after a kill -9 on a PVC, operator probe timing at that size. E2E continuous-replication-sustained (evaluation, FLARE_E2E_SUSTAINED): three steady write rates for four minutes each, sampling lag, both RSS figures, the master's WAL and data-dir bytes and the tombstone count every 30 s, then the drain after the load stops. E2E continuous-replication-outage (evaluation, FLARE_E2E_OUTAGE): ~150 MB then ~400 MB written while the replica is cut under a 256 MB WAL cap; phase A must catch up from the cursor with no reconstruction, phase B must be told lsn_purged once the archive has been purged and be rebuilt; live/archived WAL, SST count, data dir and RSS sampled every 50 MB. T17 (2026-10-02, evaluation pending): in every 30 s sustained window the evaluation also times 50 single gets against the replica and the master from the debug pod while the load runs (p50/p99/max, an upper bound because each includes starting nc), the operator's mean reconcile duration over the window from its own histogram, and the age of the operator lease. Recorded, not asserted: the bounds are for the user to set from production traffic. tmpfs variant (2026-10-02, evaluation pending): evaluation=outage-tmpfs runs the same two outage phases with the data dir in a memory-backed emptyDir (3Gi, memory limit 4Gi), so the WAL archive and the data count against the pod's memory. T17 lock hold (2026-10-02, evaluation pending): flared now exports repl_apply_lock_count / _hold_us_total / _hold_us_max / _wait_us_max (the follower's exclusive WAL-batch apply) and repl_forward_lock_wait_us_max (forwarded writes waiting on that lock), also as flare_node_repl_* metrics; the sustained evaluation prints them at the end.

Production enablement path, live (E2E continuous-replication-enable, failover-data leg): a RocksDB cluster on a PVC starts with NO follow settings, like production today; 200 keys written. Through the CR, identity forwarding is switched on (both nodes must log the reload), 100 more keys; then following (the replica must reach 'following'; the states it passes through and whether a rebuild happened are recorded), 100 more keys; then rolled back in reverse order (follow off, 50 keys; identity off, 50 keys). After each step curr_items must match and sampled values must be equal on both copies; the master must not move and the operator must log no failover, promotion, drain or breaker trip.

E2E continuous-replication-enable-purged (topology leg): legacy PVC cluster with a 4 MB write buffer, WAL TTL 60 s and size cap 16 MB; 100 keys plus ~60 MB of 50 kB values written in legacy mode, 90 s for the TTL, more writes; then identity forwarding and following are enabled through the CR. The replica must be rebuilt once (reconstruction_started +1; lsn_purged recorded if seen), then follow with items and sampled values equal; the master must not move.

E2E continuous-replication-multipart-enable (failover-data leg): a legacy 2p x 2r PVC cluster; 300 keys; identity forwarding then following switched on through the CR (all four nodes must log the reload); both partitions' replicas must follow; 200 more keys; each partition's replica must match its master's items, sampled values equal via both replicas, 500 keys in total, and neither master may move.

constraint.text: The applied position is contiguous and crash-atomic, and no other path may advance it.

controls.title: Contiguous, crash-atomic applied position
scenarios: A forwarded change applied through the rule leaves the cursor unchanged; a WAL batch whose base is beyond cursor+1 is refused; an empty batch does not move the position; a metadata-only batch advances it; the cursor Put is in the same WriteBatch as the changes, metadata and tombstones.
assumptions: RocksDB WriteBatch atomicity holds across the data and metadata column families.
residual_risks: The E2E crash lands at whatever boundary the kill hits (~300 ms after the heal); it is not steered to a specific mid-batch point. Recovery is observed through the operator's rejoin (Slave/Prepare, incremental WAL reconstruction from the cursor, activation, follower resume), so the design's 'plain restart resumes with no rebuild' (T16) holds for the data path (no truncate, no dump) but a reconstruction record is produced.

2026-10-06 (implemented in f096882, CI pending; NOT reviewed). D6: the WAL server path read the DB handle with no lock (get_updates_since, get_latest_sequence_number) while snapshot swap, hard_reset and truncate replace or reopen it under the whole-lock (write). This is reachable, for example, on a demoted master still serving in-flight follow requests while it is reseeded. Both now hold the whole-lock for read, with RAII on every return path; writers also take it for read, so serving a follower does not block writes. D7: stop_wal_follower is an asynchronous shutdown that does not wait. A stopped handler could finish a slice after its successor started; epoch, incarnation and contiguity do not catch a stale stream from a demoted master still serving the same epoch. Every stop/start now bumps a follow generation, and a batch with an older generation is refused under the apply lock with nothing written. The handler thread's lifetime is unchanged (pooled thread, no awaited join); a blocking stop under the cluster lock was rejected for deadlock risk.

constraint.text: History loss is an explicit rebuild state.

controls.title: History loss is an explicit rebuild state
scenarios: The source answers lsn_purged, epoch_mismatch, master_id_mismatch or the cursor is ahead of the source: the follower declares needs_rebuild with the reason and stops; the operator turns the declaration into a repair-ledger request (no drop counter needed) and runs demote -> hold -> reseat -> reconstruction; an incomplete snapshot restore (sentinel present) refuses to open; a copy in needs_rebuild/initial_sync is unfit for promotion.
assumptions: flared reports the follower state truthfully in stats; the operator can read it (an unreadable state is Unknown, not synchronised).
residual_risks: A follower that declares needs_rebuild in the window between a completed reconstruction and its follower restart could be requested twice (bounded churn, not loss).

Until 325a2f8 the follower handler RETURNED on needs_rebuild, giving its thread back to the pool while cluster still referenced it; the later stop_wal_follower shut down a pooled thread, which exited without leaving the pool, and the reconstruction handler that was to rebuild the node was triggered on that dead thread and never ran (found by the SAF-10d bulk-operation scenario, runs 3-4). Fixed: terminal outcomes park the thread until the controller's shutdown. E2E confirmation pending (run 5).

After a source-epoch change the master's forwarded ops are refused by the stale-session replica, retried and counted as drops, so in the E2E the DROP path requested the rebuild before the follower-declared request could (runs 5-6: entry with drops=2). The two paths race and converge on the same rebuild; the follower-declared path alone (no drop counted, e.g. a purge with no write traffic) is unit-pinned, not staged end to end.

RocksDB does not always report a purged position as NotFound: with the requested WAL file gone, GetUpdatesSince serves from the oldest surviving file. Before 3b7f38c the follower refused that first batch as a contiguity violation mapped to a TRANSIENT apply error and retried it forever (T6 E2E: state=error/apply_error, applied position frozen while forwarding delivered). Fixed: the server answers lsn_purged when the first served batch is beyond lsn+1, and the client maps a gap refusal to lsn_purged → needs_rebuild. E2E confirmation (T6 purge suite) pending.

The two routes to a rebuild request (a counted drop and the follower's own needs_rebuild declaration) have each been OBSERVED to win in E2E and both orders are pinned sequentially by flare_unit, but true concurrency is NOT verified: nothing exercises them racing within one reconcile pass against the real persist path.
lsn_purged after an actual size-cap purge (not the 1 MB/1 s harness knobs) is now staged once: outage run 3 (6e757cb) — declared and rebuilt in 59 s. Single execution.

2026-10-02 (CI 36904379135): T6 passed with exactly one reconstruction (1->2) and at most one ledger entry, but the master counted no dropped forwards during the cut (0->0), so only the follower route fired: the concurrent case of both repair triggers was NOT shown by this run.

2026-10-02 (CI 36922262408): the concurrent case is now shown. With the cut kept until the master counted dropped forwards (0->2), BOTH repair routes logged a request for the same replica in the same run (drop route and follower needs_rebuild), the ledger held at most one entry, and exactly one reconstruction started and completed (1->2), none more within 30 s. One run.

2026-10-04, found by reading pf-dev (read-only) and the code: a physical reseed stages the source's copy in snapshot.recv.tmp NEXT TO the replica's own and swaps at the end, so a live rebuild needs room for two copies, with no free-space check. On tmpfs that room is RAM charged to the container's memory cgroup: pf-dev's replica holds 5.6 GB in an 8Gi pod (tmpfs sizeLimit = memory limit = 8Gi, container already at 6.67 GB on the master), so any live rebuild there would be OOM-killed mid-transfer on every retry. Fix: before staging (the truncate window — slave, source reachable and newer; the fallback truncates anyway), flared compares the local copy (+10% +64 MiB) with the space available (filesystem free and, on tmpfs, cgroup memory.max − memory.current − 256 MiB) and, when two copies do not fit, discards the stale copy with hard_reset() first (rocksdb_rebuild_stale_discarded). Cost: during the transfer the replica holds nothing; if the source dies then, that stale copy is no longer a last-resort partial copy. Peak is still one full copy plus flared: a tmpfs sized below ~1.1× data + flared + 256 MiB cannot be rebuilt at all. CI pending.

2026-10-04 (PR run 37135485637 on 467e947, all 8 legs green; nix-linux 37135485646 green): space-aware rebuild PASS. tmpfs = memory limit = 384Mi; the replica held 136 MB (2,550 keys, ~120 MB incompressible). On enabling following it went idle → needs_rebuild(lsn_purged) → following; flared logged 'the new copy will not fit next to ours (local copy 133278373 bytes, available 0 incl. memory headroom on tmpfs) -> discarding this replica's stale copy before staging'; rocksdb_rebuild_stale_discarded 0→1, snapshot bootstraps 1→2, container restarts 0→0; items and sampled values equal; master unchanged. The cgroup-headroom path decided (available 0), not the filesystem free space.

2026-10-05, observed LIVE on pf-dev during the rc56 → rc64 roll (moc2-k8s#9362, test data), classified as FUNCTIONAL (flared, mixed-version upgrade): the new rc64 replica (nodes-1, empty tmpfs) pulled a snapshot from the rc56 master; the checkpoint carries no source epoch (rc56 predates epochs) and swap_in_snapshot refused it — but only AFTER renaming it over the local DB. The replica kept the source's ~5 GB, the fallback truncate (a key-by-key delete) freed no space, the full dump wrote a second copy, and the container was OOMKilled (exit 137) on every retry; on restart the interrupted-restore sentinel discarded the DB and the cycle repeated (2 restarts in 15 min). The StatefulSet roll stalled with nodes-0 still rc56 and serving. No E2E had rolled a running cluster from a released version. Fix: the source-epoch check moved into the read-only pre-swap probe (refused before the point of no return, local DB untouched), and the snapshot client removes its staging dir after any failed or refused bootstrap. E2E continuous-replication-upgrade starts on the released rc56 images and rolls to the build under test on tmpfs = memory limit. CI pending; pf-dev to be fixed by the next rc.

2026-10-05 (PR run 37265042480 on fa92582), classified as HARNESS: the fix held — the rc-test replica logged 'the staged checkpoint carries no source epoch ... refusing BEFORE the swap; the local DB is untouched', fell back to truncate + full dump (2,450 items), went Active, and the roll completed in 70 s. The test failed its no-restart assertion: the new replica exited 255 about one second after start, three times, then started. The test had rolled the operator and the StatefulSet at the same moment; flared exits at startup when it cannot register with the operator (cluster.cc startup_node, 'failed to connect to index server'), so it crash-looped until the new operator was up. The test now rolls the operator first, waits until it answers node sync, then rolls the StatefulSet, and additionally fails on any OOMKilled termination. Re-run pending.

constraint.text: Both delivery paths apply through one comparison rule; no path may reorder, duplicate or resurrect, and every path that can change a key participates in the label capture.

controls.title: One comparison rule for both delivery paths
scenarios: Forwarded newer value then older WAL delivery leaves the newer value; the same change by both paths is applied once; a foreign session or stale incarnation is refused; a snapshot restore clears inherited metadata; the order label is captured under the slot lock for set/remove/incr; truncate/flush_all advance the source epoch instead of labelling; concurrent forwarded and WAL delivery decide under one lock; intra-batch repetition decides against the in-batch overlay; a batch with an unsupported operation or a count mismatch is refused.
assumptions: Every per-key write path in flared goes through set/remove (incr via set) so the label capture is complete; any new path must be added to the capture or switch the epoch.
residual_risks: Lock-hold time, forwarded-write wait and writer starvation under a far-behind replica are NOT measured (T17 deferred by agreement).
E2E coexistence scenarios T10-T13 are pinned by unit tests only; the minimal E2E shows forwarding-first then WAL re-delivery skipped.

2026-10-06 (implemented in f096882, CI pending; first compile in CI; NOT reviewed). Pre-existing defects from the WSTR-0 audit (docs/design-wal-stream-wstr0.md §3), fixed on the CURRENT hybrid path. D1 (an instance of UCA-31): a replica's get() deleted an entry it judged expired by its own clock, outside the replication history; now only the partition master deletes (set on role change); a replica hides the value, counted in rocksdb_expire_filtered. D2: a follow reply with a batch but no EPOCH line was applied verbatim; it is now refused (client_no_epoch) with no data or cursor change. Verbatim apply stays for reconstruction only; legacy reconstruction compatibility is a separate path. D3: unguarded lexical_cast of LSN/BATCH; malformed, overflowing, or out-of-range batch sizes ([12 B, 1 GiB], checked before allocation) are now protocol errors with nothing applied. Not yet addressed: D4 (mid-frame failures leave the client result at its default), D5, D8-D11.
controls.call_path: Master: set/remove capture entry.seq_label inside the slot lock -> queue_proxy_write stamps rl=<epoch>/<label> when repl-identity-forward is on -> op_set/op_delete send it. Replica: entry::parse reads rl= -> storage::apply_identified_change -> storage_rocksdb::apply_forwarded_change (shared apply lock + slot lock) -> _decide_change (session, cursor, per-key label) -> WriteBatch. WAL path: apply_wal_batch (exclusive) -> same _decide_change with in-batch overlays.
